11044 — Warrād, the scribe of al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, narrated:
Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah dictated to me in a letter addressed to Muʿāwiyah that the Prophet ﷺ would say after every obligatory prayer:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things. O Allah, none can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and no person’s wealth or worldly fortune can benefit him against You.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (844) and Muslim (593).
Regarding the phrase “no person’s worldly fortune can benefit him against You,” al-Nawawī said:
“The well-known reading adopted by the majority is with the letter jīm carrying a fatḥah. Its meaning is that the wealth and good fortune of a wealthy and fortunate person cannot benefit him against You.”
Here, dubur means immediately after the prayer, as will appear in the narration of Ibn al-Zubayr.

١١٠٤٤ — عن وراد، كاتب المغيرة بن شعبة، قال: أملى علي المغيرة بن شعبة في كتاب إلى معاوية أن النبي ﷺ كان يقول في دبر كل صلاة مكتوبة: ((لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، وهو على كل شيء قدير. اللهم لا مانع لما أعطيت، ولا معطي لما منعت، ولا ينفع ذا الجد منك الجد)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٨٤٤)، ومسلم (٥٩٣).
وقوله: ((ولا ينفع ذا الجد منك الجد))، قال النووي: المشهور الذي عليه الجمهور أنه بفتح الجيم، ومعناه: لا ينفع ذا الغنى والحظ منك غناه. انتهى. ودبر هنا بمعنى عقب الصلاة، كما سيأتي في حديث ابن الزبير.

١١٠٤٦ — عن أبي الزبير قال: كان ابن الزبير يقول في دبر كل صلاة حين يسلم: ((لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، وهو على كل شيء قدير. لا حول ولا قوة إلا باللّٰه، لا إله إلا اللّٰه، ولا نعبد إلا إياه، له النعمة وله الفضل وله الثناء الحسن. لا إله إلا اللّٰه مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون)).
وقال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يهلل بهن دبر كل صلاة.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٥٩٤).

11046 — Abū al-Zubayr narrated:
Ibn al-Zubayr would say after every prayer, once he had concluded it with the greeting of peace:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things. There is no power and no strength except through Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and we worship none but Him. To Him belong all blessings, all favor, and all excellent praise. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, sincerely devoting the religion to Him, even though the disbelievers dislike it.”
He said:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to proclaim Allah’s oneness with these words after every prayer.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (594).

١١٠٤٧ — عن معاذ بن جبل أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أخذ بيده وقال: ((يا معاذ، واللّٰه إني لأحبك، واللّٰه إني لأحبك)). فقال: ((أوصيك يا معاذ، لا تدعن في دبر كل صلاة أن تقول: اللهم أعني على ذكرك وشكرك وحسن عبادتك)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٥٢٢)، وهذا لفظه، والنسائي (١٣٠٣).

11047 — Muʿādh ibn Jabal narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took him by the hand and said:
“O Muʿādh, by Allah, I truly love you. By Allah, I truly love you.”
He then said:
“I advise you, O Muʿādh: never neglect to say after every prayer, ‘O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You, and worship You in the best manner.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1522), whose wording is cited here, and al-Nasāʾī (1303).

١١٠٤٨ — عن أبي مروان أن كعبًا حلف له باللّٰه الذي فلق البحر لموسى: إنا لنجد في التوراة أن داود نبي اللّٰه كان إذا انصرف من صلاته قال: اللهم أصلح لي ديني الذي جعلته لي عصمة، وأصلح لي دنياي التي جعلت فيها معاشي. اللهم إني أعوذ برضاك من سخطك، وأعوذ بعفوك من نقمتك، وأعوذ بك منك. لا مانع لما أعطيت، ولا معطي لما منعت، ولا ينفع ذا الجد منك الجد.
قال: وحدثني كعب أن صهيبًا حدثه أن محمدًا ﷺ كان يقولهن عند انصرافه من صلاته.
حسن: رواه النسائي (١٣٤٦)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (٧٤٥)، وابن حبان (٢٠٣٦).

11048 — Abū Marwān narrated:
Kaʿb swore to him by Allah, who split the sea for Moses:
“We find in the Torah that David, the Prophet of Allah, would say after completing his prayer:
‘O Allah, rectify for me my religion, which You have made a protection for me, and rectify for me my worldly life, in which You have placed my livelihood. O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in You from You. None can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and no person’s wealth or worldly fortune can benefit him against You.’”
He said:
Kaʿb also told me that Ṣuhayb narrated to him that Muḥammad ﷺ would say these words after completing his prayer.
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (1346), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (745) and Ibn Ḥibbān (2036).

حسن: رواه النسائي (١٣٤٦)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (٧٤٥)، وابن حبان (٢٠٣٦).
11048 — Abū Marwān narrated:
Kaʿb swore to him by Allah, who split the sea for Moses:
“We find in the Torah that David, the Prophet of Allah, would say after completing his prayer:
‘O Allah, rectify for me my religion, which You have made a protection for me, and rectify for me my worldly life, in which You have placed my livelihood. O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in You from You. None can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and no person’s wealth or worldly fortune can benefit him against You.’”
He said:
Kaʿb also told me that Ṣuhayb narrated to him that Muḥammad ﷺ would say these words after completing his prayer.
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (1346), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (745) and Ibn Ḥibbān (2036).

١١٠٤٩ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص أنه كان يعلم بنيه هؤلاء الكلمات كما يعلم المعلم الغلمان الكتابة، ويقول: إن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان يتعوذ منهن دبر الصلاة: ((اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الجبن، وأعوذ بك أن أرد إلى أرذل العمر، وأعوذ بك من فتنة الدنيا، وأعوذ بك من عذاب القبر)).
وزاد في رواية: ((وأعوذ بك من البخل)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٨٢٢).
والدبر هنا بمعنى آخر الصلاة قبل التسليم.

11049 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ used to teach his sons these words just as a teacher teaches children to write. He would say:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge through them at the end of the prayer:
“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from cowardice. I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most feeble stage of life. I seek refuge in You from the trial of this world, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave.”
Another narration adds:
“And I seek refuge in You from miserliness.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2822).
Here, dubur means at the end of the prayer before the concluding greeting of peace.

١١٠٥٠ — عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: كان النبي ﷺ إذا سلم من الصلاة قال: ((اللهم اغفر لي ما قدمت، وما أخرت، وما أسررت، وما أعلنت، وما أسرفت، وما أنت أعلم به مني. أنت المقدم، وأنت المؤخر، لا إله إلا أنت)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٥٠٩).
وورد في صحيح مسلم (٧٧١/٢٠١) أن النبي ﷺ كان يقول ذلك بين التشهد والتسليم، وفي رواية أخرى: وإذا سلم. فيحمل هذا على أنه كان يقوله مرة بين التشهد والتسليم، وأخرى بعد التسليم.

english_source:
11050 — ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated:
When the Prophet ﷺ concluded the prayer with the greeting of peace, he would say:
“O Allah, forgive me for what I have sent ahead and what I have left behind, what I have concealed and what I have made public, what I have committed excessively, and what You know better about me than I do. You are the One who brings forward, and You are the One who delays. There is no deity worthy of worship except You.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1509).
It is also narrated in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (771/201) that the Prophet ﷺ would say this between the tashahhud and the concluding greeting of peace, while another narration states that he said it after concluding the prayer. These reports may be reconciled by understanding that he sometimes said it before the greeting of peace and at other times afterward.

١١٠٥١ — عن مسلم بن أبي بكرة قال: كان أبي يقول في دبر الصلاة: ((اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الكفر، والفقر، وعذاب القبر)). فكنت أقولهن. فقال أبي: أي بني، عمن أخذت هذا؟ قلت: عنك. قال: إن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان يقولهن في دبر الصلاة.
حسن: رواه النسائي (١٣٤٧)، وأحمد (٢٠٤٠٩، ٢٠٤٤٧)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (٧٤٧)، والحاكم (١/٢٥٢).
والدبر هنا بمعنى آخر الصلاة قبل التسليم.

english_source:
11051 — Muslim ibn Abī Bakrah narrated:
My father would say at the end of the prayer:
“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief, poverty, and the punishment of the grave.”
I began saying these words as well.
My father asked:
“My son, from whom did you learn this?”
I replied:
“From you.”
He said:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say these words at the end of the prayer.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (1347) and Aḥmad (20409, 20447), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (747) and al-Ḥākim (1/252).
Here, dubur means at the end of the prayer before the concluding greeting of peace.

حسن: رواه أحمد (١٨٠٦٥).

I prayed behind the Prophet ﷺ during the Year of the Conquest and heard him say:
“O Allah, do not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (18065).

١١٠٥٣ — عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء الفقراء إلى النبي ﷺ فقالوا: ذهب أهل الدثور من الأموال بالدرجات العلى والنعيم المقيم؛ يصلون كما نصلي، ويصومون كما نصوم، ولهم فضل من أموال يحجون بها ويعتمرون، ويجاهدون ويتصدقون.
قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((ألا أحدثكم بأمر إن أخذتم به أدركتم من سبقكم، ولم يدرككم أحد بعدكم، وكنتم خير من أنتم بين ظهرانيه، إلا من عمل مثله؟ تسبحون وتحمدون وتكبرون خلف كل صلاة ثلاثًا وثلاثين)).
فاختلفنا بيننا، فقال بعضنا: نسبح ثلاثًا وثلاثين، ونحمد ثلاثًا وثلاثين، ونكبر أربعًا وثلاثين. فرجعت إليه، فقال: ((تقول: سبحان اللّٰه، والحمد للّٰه، واللّٰه أكبر، حتى يكون منهن كلهن ثلاثًا وثلاثين)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٨٤٣)، ومسلم (٥٩٥)، واللفظ للبخاري.
وقوله: «الدثور»، بضم المهملة والمثلثة، جمع دثر، بفتح ثم سكون، وهو المال الكثير. وقوله: «فاختلفنا بيننا»، القائل هو سمي. وقوله: «فرجعت إليه»، أي: إلى أبي صالح، كما تدل عليه بعض روايات مسلم.

11053 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The poor came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“The wealthy have taken the highest ranks and everlasting bliss. They pray as we pray and fast as we fast, but they possess surplus wealth through which they perform pilgrimage and ʿumrah, strive in Allah’s path, and give charity.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Shall I not tell you of something through which, if you act upon it, you will catch up with those who have preceded you, no one after you will catch up with you, and you will be the best among those around you—except someone who does the same? Glorify Allah, praise Him, and proclaim His greatness thirty-three times after every prayer.”
The narrators then differed among themselves. Some said:
“We should glorify Allah thirty-three times, praise Him thirty-three times, and proclaim His greatness thirty-four times.”
I returned to him, and he said:
“Say: ‘Glory be to Allah, all praise belongs to Allah, and Allah is the Greatest,’ until each of them has been said thirty-three times.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (843) and Muslim (595). The wording cited here is that of al-Bukhārī.
The word al-duthūr is the plural of dathr and means abundant wealth.
The words “we differed among ourselves” were spoken by Sumayy.
The phrase “I returned to him” means that he returned to Abū Ṣāliḥ, as indicated by some of Muslim’s narrations.
In summary, the phrase “thirty-three times” could be understood as referring to a combined total for all three remembrances, in which case each would be said eleven times. This was the understanding of Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ, as Muslim narrated. However, he was not supported in that interpretation.
The clearer meaning is that each remembrance has its own number: Allah is glorified thirty-three times, praised thirty-three times, and magnified thirty-four times, completing one hundred. This interpretation is supported by the other narrations.
The word khalf here means after the concluding greeting of peace.

11054 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever glorifies Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, praises Allah thirty-three times, and proclaims Allah’s greatness thirty-three times—making ninety-nine—and completes the hundred by saying, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things,’ his sins will be forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (597).
Here, dubur means immediately after the prayer.

١١٠٥٥ — عن أبي ذر قال: يا رسول اللّٰه، ذهب أصحاب الدثور بالأجور، يصلون كما نصلي، ويصومون كما نصوم، ولهم فضول أموال يتصدقون بها، وليس لنا مال نتصدق به.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((يا أبا ذر، ألا أعلمك كلمات تدرك بهن من سبقك، ولا يلحقك من خلفك إلا من أخذ بمثل عملك؟)). قال: بلى يا رسول اللّٰه. قال: ((تكبر اللّٰه عز وجل دبر كل صلاة ثلاثًا وثلاثين، وتحمده ثلاثًا وثلاثين، وتسبحه ثلاثًا وثلاثين، وتختمها بلا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، وهو على كل شيء قدير، غفرت له ذنوبه ولو كانت مثل زبد البحر)).

١١٠٥٦ — عن كعب بن عجرة، عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: ((معقبات لا يخيب قائلهن - أو فاعلهن - دبر كل صلاة مكتوبة: ثلاث وثلاثون تسبيحة، وثلاث وثلاثون تحميدة، وأربع وثلاثون تكبيرة)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٥٩٦).
قوله: «معقبات»، قال الهروي: قال شمر: معناه تسبيحات تفعل أعقاب الصلاة. وقال أبو الهيثم: سميت معقبات لأنها تفعل مرة بعد أخرى. وقوله تعالى: ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ [الرعد: ١١]، أي: ملائكة يعقب بعضهم بعضًا. كذا قال النووي. والدبر بمعنى عقب الصلاة.

11056 — Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“There are remembrances recited in succession whose speaker—or performer—will not be disappointed after every obligatory prayer: thirty-three glorifications, thirty-three praises, and thirty-four proclamations of Allah’s greatness.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (596).
Regarding the word muʿaqqibāt, al-Harawī narrated from Shamir that it means glorifications recited after the prayer.
Abū al-Haytham said that they are called muʿaqqibāt because they are performed repeatedly, one after another.
Allah, the Exalted, said:
“For him are successive angels before him and behind him.”
 [Sūrat al-Raʿd 13:11]
That is, angels who follow one another in succession. This was mentioned by al-Nawawī.
Here, dubur means immediately after the prayer.

١١٠٥٧ — عن زيد بن ثابت قال: أمرنا أن نسبح دبر كل صلاة ثلاثًا وثلاثين، ونحمد ثلاثًا وثلاثين، ونكبره أربعًا وثلاثين. قال: فرأى رجل من الأنصار في المنام، فقيل له: أمركم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن تسبحوا في دبر كل صلاة ثلاثًا وثلاثين، وتحمدوا اللّٰه ثلاثًا وثلاثين، وتكبروا أربعًا وثلاثين؟ قال: نعم. قال: فاجعلوها خمسًا وعشرين، واجعلوا التهليل معهن. فغدا على النبي ﷺ فحدثه، فقال: ((افعلوا)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٣٤١٣)، والنسائي (١٣٥٠)، وأحمد (٢١٦٠٠)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (٧٥٢).
وقوله: «فاجعلوها خمسًا وعشرين»، أي: التسبيح خمس وعشرون، والتحميد خمس وعشرون، والتكبير خمس وعشرون، ولا إله إلا اللّٰه خمس وعشرون، فتلك مائة. والدبر بمعنى عقب الصلاة.

11057 — Zayd ibn Thābit narrated:
We were commanded to glorify Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, praise Him thirty-three times, and proclaim His greatness thirty-four times.
A man from the Anṣār then saw in a dream that he was asked:
“Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ command you to glorify Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, praise Him thirty-three times, and proclaim His greatness thirty-four times?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
He was told:
“Make each of them twenty-five times and include the declaration that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah among them.”
The next morning, he went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about it.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Do so.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3413), al-Nasāʾī (1350), and Aḥmad (21600), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (752).
The instruction “make them twenty-five” means to say each of the following twenty-five times: Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, Allāhu akbar, and lā ilāha illā Allāh. This makes a total of one hundred.
Here, dubur means immediately after the prayer.

وقوله: «فاجعلوها خمسًا وعشرين»، أي: التسبيح خمس وعشرون، والتحميد خمس وعشرون، والتكبير خمس وعشرون، ولا إله إلا اللّٰه خمس وعشرون، فتلك مائة. والدبر بمعنى عقب الصلاة.
11057 — Zayd ibn Thābit narrated:
We were commanded to glorify Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, praise Him thirty-three times, and proclaim His greatness thirty-four times.
A man from the Anṣār then saw in a dream that he was asked:
“Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ command you to glorify Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, praise Him thirty-three times, and proclaim His greatness thirty-four times?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
He was told:
“Make each of them twenty-five times and include the declaration that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah among them.”
The next morning, he went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about it.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Do so.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3413), al-Nasāʾī (1350), and Aḥmad (21600), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (752).
The instruction “make them twenty-five” means to say each of the following twenty-five times: Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, Allāhu akbar, and lā ilāha illā Allāh. This makes a total of one hundred.
Here, dubur means immediately after the prayer.

١١٠٥٨ — عن ابن عمر أن رجلًا رأى فيما يرى النائم، فقيل له: بأي شيء أمركم نبيكم ﷺ؟ قال: أمرنا أن نسبح ثلاثًا وثلاثين، ونحمد ثلاثًا وثلاثين، ونكبر أربعًا وثلاثين، فتلك مائة. قال: سبحوا خمسًا وعشرين، واحمدوا خمسًا وعشرين، وكبروا خمسًا وعشرين، وهللوا خمسًا وعشرين، فتلك مائة. فلما أصبح ذكر ذلك للنبي ﷺ، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((افعلوا كما قال الأنصاري)).
حسن: رواه النسائي (١٣٥١).

11058 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated:
A man saw in a dream that he was asked:
“What has your Prophet ﷺ commanded you to do?”
He replied:
“He commanded us to glorify Allah thirty-three times, praise Him thirty-three times, and proclaim His greatness thirty-four times, making one hundred.”

“Glorify Allah twenty-five times, praise Him twenty-five times, proclaim His greatness twenty-five times, and declare His oneness twenty-five times. That makes one hundred.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do as the Anṣārī said.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (1351).

١١٠٥٩ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((خصلتان - أو خلتان - لا يحافظ عليهما عبد مسلم إلا دخل الجنة، هما يسير، ومن يعمل بهما قليل: يسبح في دبر كل صلاة عشرًا، ويحمد عشرًا، ويكبر عشرًا، فذلك خمسون ومائة باللسان، وألف وخمسمائة في الميزان. ويكبر أربعًا وثلاثين إذا أخذ مضجعه، ويحمد ثلاثًا وثلاثين، ويسبح ثلاثًا وثلاثين، فذلك مائة باللسان، وألف في الميزان)).
فلقد رأيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يعقدها بيده. قالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، كيف هما يسير ومن يعمل بهما قليل؟ قال: ((يأتي أحدكم - يعني الشيطان - في منامه، فينومه قبل أن يقولها، ويأتيه في صلاته، فيذكره حاجة قبل أن يقولها)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٦٥)، والترمذي (٣٤١٠)، والنسائي (١٣٤٨)، وابن ماجه (٩٢٦).
وقوله: «فذلك خمسون ومائة»، يعني في خمس صلوات في كل يوم وليلة. والدبر بمعنى عقب الصلاة.

english_source:
11059 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“There are two practices which no Muslim servant preserves except that he will enter Paradise. They are easy, yet those who perform them are few.
After every prayer, he glorifies Allah ten times, praises Him ten times, and proclaims His greatness ten times. That amounts to one hundred and fifty upon the tongue and one thousand five hundred in the Scale.
When he goes to bed, he proclaims Allah’s greatness thirty-four times, praises Him thirty-three times, and glorifies Him thirty-three times. That amounts to one hundred upon the tongue and one thousand in the Scale.”
The narrator said:
“I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ counting them upon his hand.”
They asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how can they be easy while those who perform them are few?”
He replied:
“Satan comes to one of you when he is about to sleep and causes him to fall asleep before he says them. He also comes to him during his prayer and reminds him of some need before he says them.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5065), al-Tirmidhī (3410), al-Nasāʾī (1348), and Ibn Mājah (926).
The phrase “one hundred and fifty” refers to the total after the five daily prayers.
Here, dubur means immediately after the prayer.

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٢٣)، والنسائي (١٣٣٦)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (٧٥٥)، والحاكم (١/٢٥٣).

١١٠٦١ — عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((من قرأ آية الكرسي في دبر كل صلاة مكتوبة، لم يمنعه من دخول الجنة إلا أن يموت)).

11061 — Abū Umāmah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever recites Āyat al-Kursī after every obligatory prayer, nothing prevents him from entering Paradise except that he must die.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (100).
Here, dubur means immediately after the prayer.

“Whoever recites Āyat al-Kursī after every obligatory prayer, nothing prevents him from entering Paradise except that he must die.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (100).

١١٠٦١ — عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((من قرأ آية الكرسي في دبر كل صلاة مكتوبة، لم يمنعه من دخول الجنة إلا أن يموت)).
حسن: رواه النسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (١٠٠).
والدبر بمعنى عقب الصلاة.

١١٠٦٢ — عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((من قال في دبر صلاة الغداة: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، يحيي ويميت، بيده الخير، وهو على كل شيء قدير، مائة مرة قبل أن يثني رجليه، كان يومئذ أفضل أهل الأرض، إلا من قال مثل ما قال أو زاد على ما قال)).
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الكبير (٨/٣٣٦)، والأوسط (٤٦٥٦ - مجمع البحرين)، وابن السني في عمل اليوم والليلة (١٤٣).
والدبر بمعنى عقب الصلاة.

11062 — Abū Umāmah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever says one hundred times after the dawn prayer, before moving his legs from their position: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise. He gives life and causes death. All goodness is in His hand, and He has power over all things,’ will on that day be the best of the people of the earth, except someone who says the same as he said or says more.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (8/336) and al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ (4656, as cited in Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn), and by Ibn al-Sunnī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (143).
Here, dubur means immediately after the prayer.

١١٠٦٤ — عن ابن عباس أن رفع الصوت بالذكر حين ينصرف الناس من المكتوبة كان على عهد النبي ﷺ.
وقال ابن عباس: كنت أعلم إذا انصرفوا بذلك إذا سمعته.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٨٤١)، ومسلم (٥٨٣/١٢٢).
ورواه البخاري (٨٤٢)، ومسلم (٥٨٣/١٢٠) بلفظ: كنا نعرف انقضاء صلاة رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بالتكبير.
وقوله: «بالتكبير»، المراد به الذكر كما في الرواية الأولى؛ لأن الأدعية الواردة عقب الصلوات المفروضة ليس فيها التكبير. ويحتمل أن النبي ﷺ رفع صوته بالتكبير مرة أو مرتين، فسمعه ابن عباس، ولم يكن ذلك من عادته ﷺ.

english_source:
11064 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
Raising the voice with remembrance when the people completed the obligatory prayer was practiced during the time of the Prophet ﷺ.
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“I would know that they had completed the prayer when I heard it.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (841) and Muslim (583/122).
Al-Bukhārī (842) and Muslim (583/120) also narrated it with the wording:
“We used to recognize the completion of the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by the takbīr.”
The word “takbīr” here may refer generally to remembrance, as indicated by the first narration, because the reported supplications after obligatory prayers do not contain takbīr.
It is also possible that the Prophet ﷺ raised his voice with the takbīr on one or two occasions and Ibn ʿAbbās heard it, although this was not his regular practice.

١١٠٦٥ — عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي ﷺ إذا قام من الليل يتهجد قال: ((اللهم لك الحمد، أنت قيم السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن، ولك الحمد، لك ملك السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن، ولك الحمد، أنت نور السماوات والأرض، ولك الحمد، أنت ملك السماوات والأرض، ولك الحمد، أنت الحق، ووعدك الحق، ولقاؤك حق، وقولك حق، والجنة حق، والنار حق، والنبيون حق، ومحمد حق، والساعة حق.
اللهم لك أسلمت، وبك آمنت، وعليك توكلت، وإليك أنبت، وبك خاصمت، وإليك حاكمت، فاغفر لي ما قدمت وما أخرت، وما أسررت وما أعلنت. أنت المقدم، وأنت المؤخر، لا إله إلا أنت، لا إله غيرك)).
قال سفيان: وزاد عبد الكريم أبو أمية: ((ولا حول ولا قوة إلا باللّٰه)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١١٢٠)، ومسلم (٧٦٩).

11065 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
When the Prophet ﷺ rose during the night to perform the night prayer, he would say:
“O Allah, all praise belongs to You. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and all who are within them. All praise belongs to You. To You belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all who are within them. All praise belongs to You. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth. All praise belongs to You. You are the King of the heavens and the earth.
All praise belongs to You. You are the Truth, Your promise is true, meeting You is true, Your word is true, Paradise is true, the Fire is true, the prophets are true, Muḥammad is true, and the Hour is true.
O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, upon You I have relied, to You I have turned in repentance, through Your aid I have disputed, and to You I have referred for judgment. Forgive me for what I have sent ahead and what I have left behind, what I have concealed and what I have made public. You are the One who brings forward, and You are the One who delays. There is no deity worthy of worship except You; there is no deity besides You.”
Sufyān said:
ʿAbd al-Karīm Abū Umayyah added:
“There is no power and no strength except through Allah.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1120) and Muslim (769).

١١٠٦٥ — عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي ﷺ إذا قام من الليل يتهجد قال: ((اللهم لك الحمد، أنت قيم السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن، ولك الحمد، لك ملك السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن، ولك الحمد، أنت نور السماوات والأرض، ولك الحمد، أنت ملك السماوات والأرض، ولك الحمد، أنت الحق، ووعدك الحق، ولقاؤك حق، وقولك حق، والجنة حق، والنار حق، والنبيون حق، ومحمد حق، والساعة حق.
اللهم لك أسلمت، وبك آمنت، وعليك توكلت، وإليك أنبت، وبك خاصمت، وإليك حاكمت، فاغفر لي ما قدمت وما أخرت، وما أسررت وما أعلنت. أنت المقدم، وأنت المؤخر، لا إله إلا أنت، لا إله غيرك)).
قال سفيان: وزاد عبد الكريم أبو أمية: ((ولا حول ولا قوة إلا باللّٰه)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١١٢٠)، ومسلم (٧٦٩).
11065 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
When the Prophet ﷺ rose during the night to perform the night prayer, he would say:
“O Allah, all praise belongs to You. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and all who are within them. All praise belongs to You. To You belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all who are within them. All praise belongs to You. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth. All praise belongs to You. You are the King of the heavens and the earth.
All praise belongs to You. You are the Truth, Your promise is true, meeting You is true, Your word is true, Paradise is true, the Fire is true, the prophets are true, Muḥammad is true, and the Hour is true.
O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, upon You I have relied, to You I have turned in repentance, through Your aid I have disputed, and to You I have referred for judgment. Forgive me for what I have sent ahead and what I have left behind, what I have concealed and what I have made public. You are the One who brings forward, and You are the One who delays. There is no deity worthy of worship except You; there is no deity besides You.”
Sufyān said:
ʿAbd al-Karīm Abū Umayyah added:
“There is no power and no strength except through Allah.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1120) and Muslim (769).

١١٠٦٦ — عن عبادة بن الصامت، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((من تعار من الليل فقال: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، وهو على كل شيء قدير، الحمد للّٰه، وسبحان اللّٰه، ولا إله إلا اللّٰه، واللّٰه أكبر، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا باللّٰه، ثم قال: اللهم اغفر لي، أو دعا، استجيب له، فإن توضأ وصلى قبلت صلاته)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١١٥٤).
قال البغوي: قوله: «تعار»، أي: استيقظ من النوم.

11066 — ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever awakens during the night and says: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things. All praise belongs to Allah, glory be to Allah, there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and there is no power and no strength except through Allah,’ and then says, ‘O Allah, forgive me,’ or makes another supplication, his supplication will be answered. If he performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1154).
Al-Baghawī said that the word taʿārra means to awaken from sleep.

١١٠٦٧ — عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال: سألت عائشة أم المؤمنين: بأي شيء كان نبي اللّٰه ﷺ يفتتح صلاته إذا قام من الليل؟ قالت: كان إذا قام من الليل افتتح صلاته: ((اللهم رب جبريل وميكائيل وإسرافيل، فاطر السماوات والأرض، عالم الغيب والشهادة، أنت تحكم بين عبادك فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون، اهدني لما اختلف فيه من الحق بإذنك، إنك تهدي من تشاء إلى صراط مستقيم)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٧٧٠).

11067 — Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf narrated:
I asked ʿĀʾishah, Mother of the Believers:
“With what would the Prophet of Allah ﷺ begin his prayer when he rose during the night?”
She replied:
When he rose during the night, he would begin his prayer by saying:
“O Allah, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Isrāfīl, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (770).

١١٠٦٨ — عن عاصم بن حميد قال: سألت عائشة: بأي شيء كان يفتتح رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قيام الليل؟ فقالت: لقد سألتني عن شيء ما سألني عنه أحد قبلك. كان إذا قام كبر عشرًا، وحمد اللّٰه عشرًا، وسبح عشرًا، وهلل عشرًا، واستغفر عشرًا، وقال: ((اللهم اغفر لي، واهدني، وارزقني)). ويتعوذ من ضيق المقام يوم القيامة.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٧٦٦)، والنسائي (١٦١٨)، وابن ماجه (١٣٥٦)، وصححه ابن حبان (٢٦٠٢).

11068 — ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated:
I asked ʿĀʾishah:
“With what would the Messenger of Allah ﷺ begin the night prayer?”
She replied:
“You have asked me about something that no one before you has asked me.”
When he rose, he would proclaim Allah’s greatness ten times, praise Allah ten times, glorify Him ten times, declare His oneness ten times, and seek His forgiveness ten times.
He would then say:
“O Allah, forgive me, guide me, and provide for me.”
He would also seek refuge from the constriction and hardship of standing on the Day of Resurrection.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (766), al-Nasāʾī (1618), and Ibn Mājah (1356), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (2602).

11069 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
I spent a night at the home of my maternal aunt Maymūnah. The Prophet ﷺ rose during the night, relieved himself, washed his face and hands, and then slept.
He later rose again, went to the water-skin, loosened its strap, and performed a moderate but complete ablution. He then stood to pray.
I rose and stretched, not wanting him to realize that I had been awake and observing him. I performed ablution and stood on his left side. He took me by the hand and moved me to his right.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ completed thirteen units of prayer during the night. He then lay down and slept until the sound of his breathing could be heard, for when he slept, his breathing could be heard.
Bilāl came and informed him that it was time for prayer. He rose and prayed without performing a new ablution.
Among his supplications was:
“O Allah, place light within my heart, light within my sight, and light within my hearing. Place light to my right and light to my left, light above me and light beneath me, light before me and light behind me, and magnify light for me.”
Kurayb, the narrator from Ibn ʿAbbās, said:
“There were seven additional phrases stored in my heart.”
I later met one of the descendants of al-ʿAbbās, who narrated them to me. He mentioned:
“My nerves, my flesh, my blood, my hair, and my skin,”
and he mentioned two additional qualities.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6316) and Muslim (763/181).
The phrase “in the chest” means that seven additional words were retained in his heart, but he later forgot them.

١١٠٧٠ — عن علي بن أبي طالب أن النبي ﷺ كان يقول في آخر الوتر: ((اللهم إني أعوذ برضاك من سخطك، وأعوذ بمعافاتك من عقوبتك، وأعوذ بك منك، لا أحصي ثناء عليك، أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٤٢٧)، والترمذي (٣٥٦١)، والنسائي (١٧٤٨)، وابن ماجه (١١٧٩).

11070 — ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated:
At the end of the Witr prayer, the Prophet ﷺ would say:
“O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in You from You. I cannot enumerate sufficient praise of You. You are as You have praised Yourself.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1427), al-Tirmidhī (3561), al-Nasāʾī (1748), and Ibn Mājah (1179).

11071 — Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me words to say during the Witr prayer:
“O Allah, guide me among those whom You have guided. Grant me well-being among those to whom You have granted well-being. Take me into Your care among those whom You have taken into Your care. Bless me in what You have given me, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. Indeed, You decree, and none decrees over You. The one whom You befriend is never humiliated, and the one whom You oppose is never honored. Blessed are You, our Lord, and Exalted.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1425), al-Tirmidhī (464), al-Nasāʾī (1745), and Ibn Mājah (1178).

١١٠٧٤ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: دعا النبي ﷺ على الذين قتلوا - يعني أصحابه - ببئر معونة ثلاثين صباحًا، حين يدعو على رعل ولحيان وعصية: ((عصية عصت اللّٰه ورسوله)).
قال أنس: فأنزل اللّٰه تعالى لنبيه ﷺ في الذين قتلوا - أصحاب بئر معونة - قرآنًا قرأناه حتى نسخ بعد: «بلغوا قومنا أنا قد لقينا ربنا، فرضي عنا، ورضينا عنه».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٠٩٥)، ومسلم (٦٧٧).

11074 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
For thirty mornings, the Prophet ﷺ supplicated against those who had killed his Companions at Biʾr Maʿūnah. He supplicated against Riʿl, Liḥyān, and ʿUṣayyah, saying:
“ʿUṣayyah has disobeyed Allah and His Messenger.”
Anas said:
Allah, the Exalted, revealed to His Prophet ﷺ concerning those Companions who had been killed at Biʾr Maʿūnah words of the Qur’an which we recited until they were later abrogated:
“Inform our people that we have met our Lord, that He is pleased with us, and that we are pleased with Him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4095) and Muslim (677).

١١٠٧٥ — عن أبي هريرة قال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول حين يفرغ من صلاة الفجر من القراءة، ويكبر، ويرفع رأسه: ((سمع اللّٰه لمن حمده، ربنا ولك الحمد)). ثم يقول وهو قائم: ((اللهم أنج الوليد بن الوليد، وسلمة بن هشام، وعياش بن أبي ربيعة، والمستضعفين من المؤمنين. اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر، واجعلها عليهم كسني يوسف. اللهم العن لحيان ورعلًا وذكوان وعصية، عصت اللّٰه ورسوله)).
ثم بلغنا أنه ترك ذلك لما أنزل: ﴿لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾ [سورة آل عمران: ١٢٨].
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٥٦٠)، ومسلم (٦٧٥).
وثبت عن عمر بن الخطاب أنه كان يقنت في الفجر، يقول:
بسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم، اللهم إنا نستعينك، ونؤمن بك، ونتوكل عليك، ونثني عليك الخير، ولا نكفرك.
ثم قرأ: بسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم، اللهم إياك نعبد، ولك نصلي ونسجد، وإليك نسعى ونحفد، نرجو رحمتك، ونخشى عذابك، إن عذابك بالكافرين ملحق. اللهم عذب كفرة أهل الكتاب الذين يصدون عن سبيلك.
رواه ابن أبي شيبة (٧١٠٤)، عن حفص بن غياث، عن ابن جريج، عن عطاء، عن عبيد بن عمير، قال: سمعت عمر يقنت في الفجر، فذكره. وإسناده صحيح، وهو موقوف على عمر بن الخطاب.

11075 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished reciting during the Fajr prayer, proclaimed the takbīr, and raised his head, he would say:
“Allah hears the one who praises Him. Our Lord, and all praise belongs to You.”
Then, while standing, he would say:
“O Allah, rescue al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd, Salamah ibn Hishām, ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, and the oppressed believers. O Allah, intensify Your punishment upon Muḍar and inflict upon them years of famine like the years of Joseph. O Allah, curse Liḥyān, Riʿl, Dhakwān, and ʿUṣayyah, for they disobeyed Allah and His Messenger.”
We were later informed that he stopped doing this when the following verse was revealed:
“You have no authority in this matter—whether He turns toward them in mercy or punishes them—for indeed, they are wrongdoers.”
 [Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:128]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4560) and Muslim (675).
It is also authentically established that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb would recite the qunūt during the Fajr prayer, saying:
“In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O Allah, we seek Your assistance, believe in You, rely upon You, praise You for all goodness, and do not disbelieve in You.”
He would then recite:
“In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O Allah, You alone we worship. For You we pray and prostrate. Toward You we hasten and strive. We hope for Your mercy and fear Your punishment. Indeed, Your punishment will overtake the disbelievers. O Allah, punish the disbelievers among the People of the Book who turn others away from Your path.”
Narrated by Ibn Abī Shaybah (7104), through Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said:
“I heard ʿUmar reciting the qunūt during the Fajr prayer,”
and he mentioned this supplication.
Its chain of transmission is authentic, and it is a statement attributed to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.

ثم قرأ: بسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم، اللهم إياك نعبد، ولك نصلي ونسجد، وإليك نسعى ونحفد، نرجو رحمتك، ونخشى عذابك، إن عذابك بالكافرين ملحق. اللهم عذب كفرة أهل الكتاب الذين يصدون عن سبيلك.
رواه ابن أبي شيبة (٧١٠٤)، عن حفص بن غياث، عن ابن جريج، عن عطاء، عن عبيد بن عمير، قال: سمعت عمر يقنت في الفجر، فذكره. وإسناده صحيح، وهو موقوف على عمر بن الخطاب.
11075 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished reciting during the Fajr prayer, proclaimed the takbīr, and raised his head, he would say:
“Allah hears the one who praises Him. Our Lord, and all praise belongs to You.”
Then, while standing, he would say:
“O Allah, rescue al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd, Salamah ibn Hishām, ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, and the oppressed believers. O Allah, intensify Your punishment upon Muḍar and inflict upon them years of famine like the years of Joseph. O Allah, curse Liḥyān, Riʿl, Dhakwān, and ʿUṣayyah, for they disobeyed Allah and His Messenger.”
We were later informed that he stopped doing this when the following verse was revealed:
“You have no authority in this matter—whether He turns toward them in mercy or punishes them—for indeed, they are wrongdoers.”
 [Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:128]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4560) and Muslim (675).
It is also authentically established that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb would recite the qunūt during the Fajr prayer, saying:
“In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O Allah, we seek Your assistance, believe in You, rely upon You, praise You for all goodness, and do not disbelieve in You.”
He would then recite:
“In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O Allah, You alone we worship. For You we pray and prostrate. Toward You we hasten and strive. We hope for Your mercy and fear Your punishment. Indeed, Your punishment will overtake the disbelievers. O Allah, punish the disbelievers among the People of the Book who turn others away from Your path.”
Narrated by Ibn Abī Shaybah (7104), through Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said:
“I heard ʿUmar reciting the qunūt during the Fajr prayer,”
and he mentioned this supplication.
Its chain of transmission is authentic, and it is a statement attributed to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.

١١٠٧٦ — عن عثمان بن أبي العاص أنه أتى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، إن الشيطان قد حال بيني وبين صلاتي وقراءتي، يلبسها علي. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((ذاك شيطان يقال له خنزب، فإذا أحسسته فتعوذ باللّٰه منه، واتفل على يسارك ثلاثًا)). فقال: ففعلت ذلك، فأذهبه اللّٰه عني.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٠٣).
قوله: «خنزب»، بخاء معجمة مكسورة، ثم نون ساكنة، ثم زاي مكسورة ومفتوحة، وهو لقب الشيطان، ومعناه: قطعة لحم منتنة. ومعنى: «يلبسها»، أي: يخلطها ويشككني فيها. وقوله: «حال بيني وبين صلاتي»، أي: نكدني فيها، ومنعني لذتها والفراغ للخشوع فيها. هكذا قال النووي.

11076 — ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Satan has come between me and my prayer and recitation, confusing me during them.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“That is a devil called Khinzab. When you sense him, seek refuge in Allah from him and spit lightly to your left three times.”
He said:
“I did that, and Allah removed him from me.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2203).
The name Khinzab begins with a kasrah on the letter khāʾ, followed by a silent nūn, and then a zāy that may be pronounced with either a kasrah or a fatḥah. It is a name given to this devil, and its literal meaning is a piece of foul-smelling flesh.
The phrase “confusing me during it” means that he mixes up the prayer and causes doubt concerning it.
The words “he has come between me and my prayer” mean that he disturbed the prayer, deprived the worshipper of its sweetness, and prevented him from attaining complete concentration and humility. This explanation was given by al-Nawawī.

١١٠٧٧ — عن أنس بن مالك أن رجلًا دخل المسجد يوم جمعة من باب كان نحو دار القضاء، ورسول اللّٰه ﷺ قائم يخطب، فاستقبل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قائمًا، ثم قال: يا رسول اللّٰه، هلكت الأموال، وانقطعت السبل، فادع اللّٰه يغيثنا.
فرفع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يديه، ثم قال: ((اللهم أغثنا، اللهم أغثنا، اللهم أغثنا)).
قال أنس: ولا واللّٰه، ما نرى في السماء من سحاب ولا قزعة، وما بيننا وبين سلع من بيت ولا دار. قال: فطلعت من ورائه سحابة مثل الترس، فلما توسطت السماء انتشرت، ثم أمطرت. فلا واللّٰه، ما رأينا الشمس ستًّا… الحديث.
وفي رواية: ((اللهم اسقنا، اللهم اسقنا، اللهم اسقنا)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٠١٤)، ومسلم (٨٩٧). والرواية الأخرى رواها البخاري (١٠١٣).

11077 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
A man entered the mosque on a Friday through a doorway facing Dār al-Qaḍāʾ while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing and delivering the sermon.
The man stood facing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, the wealth has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off. Supplicate to Allah to send us relief through rain.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said:
“O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain.”
Anas said:
“By Allah, we could not see a cloud or even a small patch of cloud in the sky, and there was no house or building between us and Mount Salʿ.”
A cloud then appeared from behind it like a shield. When it reached the middle of the sky, it spread and began to rain.
Anas said:
“By Allah, we did not see the sun for six days…”
This forms part of the hadith.
Another narration states:
“O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1014) and Muslim (897). The alternative wording was narrated by al-Bukhārī (1013).

قال أنس: ولا واللّٰه، ما نرى في السماء من سحاب ولا قزعة، وما بيننا وبين سلع من بيت ولا دار. قال: فطلعت من ورائه سحابة مثل الترس، فلما توسطت السماء انتشرت، ثم أمطرت. فلا واللّٰه، ما رأينا الشمس ستًّا… الحديث.
وفي رواية: ((اللهم اسقنا، اللهم اسقنا، اللهم اسقنا)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٠١٤)، ومسلم (٨٩٧). والرواية الأخرى رواها البخاري (١٠١٣).
11077 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
A man entered the mosque on a Friday through a doorway facing Dār al-Qaḍāʾ while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing and delivering the sermon.
The man stood facing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, the wealth has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off. Supplicate to Allah to send us relief through rain.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said:
“O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain.”
Anas said:
“By Allah, we could not see a cloud or even a small patch of cloud in the sky, and there was no house or building between us and Mount Salʿ.”
A cloud then appeared from behind it like a shield. When it reached the middle of the sky, it spread and began to rain.
Anas said:
“By Allah, we did not see the sun for six days…”
This forms part of the hadith.
Another narration states:
“O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1014) and Muslim (897). The alternative wording was narrated by al-Bukhārī (1013).

١١٠٧٨ — عن عائشة قالت: شكا الناس إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قحوط المطر، فأمر بمنبر، فوضع له في المصلى، ووعد الناس يومًا يخرجون فيه.
قالت عائشة: فخرج رسول اللّٰه ﷺ حين بدا حاجب الشمس، فقعد على المنبر، فكبر وحمد اللّٰه عز وجل، ثم قال: ((إنكم شكوتم جدب دياركم، واستئخار المطر عن إبان زمانه عنكم، وقد أمركم اللّٰه عز وجل أن تدعوه، ووعدكم أن يستجيب لكم)).
ثم قال: ((الحمد للّٰه رب العالمين، الرحمن الرحيم، ملك يوم الدين. لا إله إلا اللّٰه، يفعل ما يريد. اللهم أنت اللّٰه، لا إله إلا أنت، الغني ونحن الفقراء. أنزل علينا الغيث، واجعل ما أنزلت لنا قوة وبلاغًا إلى حين)).
ثم رفع يديه، فلم يزل في الرفع حتى بدا بياض إبطيه. ثم حول إلى الناس ظهره، وقلب - أو حول - رداءه، وهو رافع يديه. ثم أقبل على الناس، ونزل، فصلى ركعتين.
فأنشأ اللّٰه سحابة، فرعدت وبرقت، ثم أمطرت بإذن اللّٰه. فلم يأت المسجد حتى سالت السيول. فلما رأى سرعتهم إلى الكن ضحك ﷺ حتى بدت نواجذه، فقال: ((أشهد أن اللّٰه على كل شيء قدير، وأني عبد اللّٰه ورسوله)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١١٧٣)، وصححه ابن حبان (٢٨٦٠)، والحاكم (١/٣٢٨).

11078 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
The people complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the lack of rain. He ordered that a pulpit be placed for him at the outdoor prayer ground and appointed a day on which the people should gather.
ʿĀʾishah said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out when the edge of the sun appeared. He sat upon the pulpit, proclaimed Allah’s greatness, praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and then said:
“You have complained of drought in your lands and of the rain being delayed beyond its usual season. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you to call upon Him and has promised that He will answer you.”
He then said:
“All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful, Sovereign of the Day of Judgment. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. He does whatever He wills.
O Allah, You are Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except You. You are the Self-Sufficient, while we are the poor and needy. Send rain down upon us, and make what You send a source of strength and provision for us for a time.”
He then raised his hands and continued raising them until the whiteness of his armpits became visible.
He turned his back toward the people and reversed—or turned—his cloak while continuing to raise his hands. He then faced the people, descended, and prayed two units.
Allah then formed a cloud. It thundered and flashed with lightning, and rain fell by Allah’s permission.
The Prophet ﷺ had not yet reached the mosque before streams began flowing.
When he saw the people hurrying toward shelter, he laughed until his molar teeth became visible and said:
“I testify that Allah has power over all things and that I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1173), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (2860) and al-Ḥākim (1/328).

١١٠٧٩ — عن شرحبيل بن السمط أنه قال لكعب: يا كعب بن مرة، حدثنا عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ واحذر. قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، استسق اللّٰه. فرفع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يديه فقال: ((اللهم اسقنا غيثًا مريئًا مريعًا طبقًا عاجلًا غير رائث، نافعًا غير ضار)).
قال: فما جمعوا حتى أحيوا. قال: فأتوه فشكوا إليه المطر، فقالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، تهدمت البيوت. فقال: ((اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا)). قال: فجعل السحاب ينقطع يمينًا وشمالًا.
صحيح: رواه ابن ماجه (١٢٦٩)، وأحمد (١٨٠٦١)، والحاكم (١/٣٢٨).
قوله: ((مريعًا))، بفتح أوله: المخصب الناجع، يقال: أمرع الوادي، ومرع مراعة. وقوله: ((طبقًا))، بفتحتين: عامًا واسعًا مالئًا للأرض، مغطيًا لها كالطبق. وقوله: ((غير رائث))، أي: غير متأخر ولا بطيء.

11079 — Shuraḥbīl ibn al-Simṭ said to Kaʿb:
“O Kaʿb ibn Murrah, narrate to us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but be cautious and precise.”
Kaʿb said:
A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to send us rain.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said:
“O Allah, send us wholesome, fertile, widespread rain, swiftly and without delay—beneficial and not harmful.”
Before the people had dispersed, the land had been revived.
They later came to him complaining about the abundance of rain and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, the houses have collapsed.”
He said:
“O Allah, let it fall around us and not upon us.”
The clouds then began breaking apart to the right and left.
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (1269), Aḥmad (18061), and al-Ḥākim (1/328).
The word murīʿan means fertile and productive. It is said that a valley has become fertile when abundant vegetation grows within it.
The word ṭabaqan means general and widespread, filling and covering the land like a lid.
The expression “without delay” means neither late nor slow in arriving.

“O Allah, send us wholesome, fertile, widespread rain, swiftly and without delay—beneficial and not harmful.”

“O Messenger of Allah, the houses have collapsed.”
He said:
“O Allah, let it fall around us and not upon us.”
The clouds then began breaking apart to the right and left.

The word murīʿan means fertile and productive. It is said that a valley has become fertile when abundant vegetation grows within it.
The word ṭabaqan means general and widespread, filling and covering the land like a lid.
The expression “without delay” means neither late nor slow in arriving.

١١٠٧٩ — عن شرحبيل بن السمط أنه قال لكعب: يا كعب بن مرة، حدثنا عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ واحذر. قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، استسق اللّٰه. فرفع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يديه فقال: ((اللهم اسقنا غيثًا مريئًا مريعًا طبقًا عاجلًا غير رائث، نافعًا غير ضار)).
قال: فما جمعوا حتى أحيوا. قال: فأتوه فشكوا إليه المطر، فقالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، تهدمت البيوت. فقال: ((اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا)). قال: فجعل السحاب ينقطع يمينًا وشمالًا.
صحيح: رواه ابن ماجه (١٢٦٩)، وأحمد (١٨٠٦١)، والحاكم (١/٣٢٨).
قوله: ((مريعًا))، بفتح أوله: المخصب الناجع، يقال: أمرع الوادي، ومرع مراعة. وقوله: ((طبقًا))، بفتحتين: عامًا واسعًا مالئًا للأرض، مغطيًا لها كالطبق. وقوله: ((غير رائث))، أي: غير متأخر ولا بطيء.

A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:

“O Messenger of Allah, the houses have collapsed.”

“O Allah, let it fall around us and not upon us.”
The clouds then began breaking apart to the right and left.
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (1269), Aḥmad (18061), and al-Ḥākim (1/328).

The word ṭabaqan means general and widespread, filling and covering the land like a lid.
The expression “without delay” means neither late nor slow in arriving.

11080 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated:
Weeping people came to the Prophet ﷺ, so he said:
“O Allah, send us relieving, wholesome, fertile, beneficial rain that causes no harm—quickly and without delay.”
The sky then became completely covered with clouds above them.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1169), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (1416) and al-Ḥākim (1/327).
The word bawākī is the plural of bākiyah, meaning that weeping people—or weeping women—came to him.

١١٠٨١ — عن ابن عباس قال: جاء أعرابي إلى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، لقد جئتك من عند قوم ما يتزود لهم راع، ولا يخطر لهم فحل. فصعد المنبر، فحمد اللّٰه، ثم قال: ((اللهم اسقنا غيثًا مغيثًا مريئًا طبقًا مريعًا غدقًا، عاجلًا غير رائث)). ثم نزل، فما يأتيه أحد من وجه من الوجوه إلا قالوا: قد أحيينا.
صحيح: رواه ابن ماجه (١٢٧٠).

english_source:
11081 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I have come to you from a people whose shepherd has nothing to take as provisions and whose male livestock no longer even moves among the herd.”
The Prophet ﷺ ascended the pulpit, praised Allah, and then said:
“O Allah, send us relieving, wholesome, widespread, fertile, abundant rain—quickly and without delay.”
He then descended.
No one came to him from any direction except that they said:
“Our land has been revived.”
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (1270).

حسن: رواه أبو داود (١١٧٦).

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sought rain, he would say:
“O Allah, give water to Your servants and Your animals, spread Your mercy, and revive Your dead land.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1176).

صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٠٣٢).
قوله: «صيبًا»، أي: منهمرًا متدفقًا، وأصله الواو، وأبدلت بالياء.

11083 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw rain, he would say:
“May it be beneficial, pouring rain.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1032).
The word ṣayyiban means rain that pours down abundantly and continuously. Its original root contains the letter wāw, which was changed into a yāʾ.

١١٠٨٤ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إذا كان يوم الريح والغيم، عرف ذلك في وجهه، وأقبل وأدبر. فإذا مطرت سر به، وذهب عنه ذلك. قالت عائشة: فسألته فقال: ((إني خشيت أن يكون عذابًا سلط على أمتي)). ويقول إذا رأى المطر: ((رحمة)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٨٩٩/١٤).

english_source:
11084 — ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated:
Whenever there was strong wind and cloud, its effect could be seen upon the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He would move forward and backward anxiously.
When rain began to fall, he became pleased and his concern disappeared.
ʿĀʾishah said:
I asked him about this, and he replied:
“I feared that it might be a punishment sent upon my nation.”
When he saw the rain, he would say:
“It is mercy.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (899/14).

١١٠٨٥ — عن أنس بن مالك أن رجلًا دخل يوم الجمعة من باب كان نحو دار القضاء، ورسول اللّٰه ﷺ قائم يخطب… الحديث.
ثم دخل رجل من ذلك الباب في الجمعة - يعني المقبلة - ورسول اللّٰه ﷺ قائم يخطب، فاستقبله قائمًا فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، هلكت الأموال، وانقطعت السبل، فادع اللّٰه يمسكها عنا.
قال: فرفع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يديه، ثم قال: ((اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا، اللهم على الآكام والظراب، وبطون الأودية، ومنابت الشجر)). قال: فأقلعت، وخرجنا نمشي في الشمس.
قال شريك: فسألت أنس بن مالك: أهو الرجل الأول؟ قال: ما أدري.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٠١٤)، ومسلم (٨٩٧).
وقوله: «على الآكام»، جمع أكمة، وهي الرابية. وقوله: «والظراب»، يعني الجبال الصغار، واحدها ظرب، على وزن كتف.

11085 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
A man entered on Friday through a doorway facing Dār al-Qaḍāʾ while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing and delivering the sermon.
The remainder of the earlier incident was then mentioned.
On the following Friday, a man entered through the same doorway while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing him and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, the wealth has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off. Supplicate to Allah to withhold the rain from us.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said:
“O Allah, let it fall around us and not upon us. O Allah, let it fall upon the hills, the small mountains, the valleys, and the places where trees grow.”
The rain then stopped, and we went out walking in the sunlight.
Sharīk said:
I asked Anas ibn Mālik:
“Was this the same man who had come the first time?”
He replied:
“I do not know.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1014) and Muslim (897).
The word ākām is the plural of akamah, meaning a raised hill.
The word ẓirāb refers to small mountains. Its singular is ẓarib.

١١٠٨٦ — عن جابر قال: كان النبي ﷺ يعلمنا الاستخارة في الأمور كلها كالسورة من القرآن: إذا هم بالأمر، فليركع ركعتين، ثم يقول: ((اللهم إني أستخيرك بعلمك، وأستقدرك بقدرتك، وأسألك من فضلك العظيم؛ فإنك تقدر ولا أقدر، وتعلم ولا أعلم، وأنت علام الغيوب.
اللهم إن كنت تعلم أن هذا الأمر خير لي في ديني ومعاشي وعاقبة أمري - أو قال: في عاجل أمري وآجله - فاقدره لي. وإن كنت تعلم أن هذا الأمر شر لي في ديني ومعاشي وعاقبة أمري - أو قال: في عاجل أمري وآجله - فاصرفه عني، واصرفني عنه، واقدر لي الخير حيث كان، ثم رضني به)). ويسمي حاجته.
وزاد في رواية: ((من غير الفريضة)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٣٨٢). والرواية الأخرى له (١١٦٢).

11086 — Jābir narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ would teach us how to seek Allah’s guidance in all matters just as he would teach us a sūrah from the Qur’an.
He said:
“When he intends to undertake a matter, let him pray two units and then say:
‘O Allah, I seek the better choice through Your knowledge, and I seek ability through Your power. I ask You from Your immense bounty, for You are able while I am not, You know while I do not, and You are the Knower of all unseen things.
O Allah, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the final outcome of my affair—or he said: in my immediate and future affairs—then decree it for me.
If You know that this matter is harmful for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the final outcome of my affair—or he said: in my immediate and future affairs—then turn it away from me and turn me away from it. Decree good for me wherever it may be, and then make me content with it.’”
He should then mention his particular need.
Another narration adds:
“Two units other than the obligatory prayer.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6382). The alternative wording is also narrated by him (1162).

١١٠٨٧ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إذا أراد أحدكم أمرًا فليقل: اللهم إني أستخيرك بعلمك، وأستقدرك بقدرتك، وأسألك من فضلك العظيم؛ فإنك تقدر ولا أقدر، وتعلم ولا أعلم، وأنت علام الغيوب.
اللهم إن كان كذا وكذا خيرًا لي في ديني، وخيرًا لي في معيشتي، وخيرًا لي في عاقبة أمري، فاقدره لي، وبارك لي فيه. وإن كان غير ذلك خيرًا لي، فاقدر لي الخير حيثما كان، ورضني بقدرك)).
حسن: رواه ابن حبان (٨٨٦)، والبخاري في التاريخ (٤/٢٥٨)، والطبراني في الدعاء (١٣٠٦).

11087 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When one of you intends to undertake a matter, let him say: ‘O Allah, I seek the better choice through Your knowledge, and I seek ability through Your power. I ask You from Your immense bounty, for You are able while I am not, You know while I do not, and You are the Knower of all unseen things.
O Allah, if such-and-such a matter is good for me in my religion, good for me in my livelihood, and good for me in the final outcome of my affair, then decree it for me and bless it for me. If something else is better for me, then decree good for me wherever it may be and make me content with Your decree.’”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān (886), al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh (4/258), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ (1306).

full_display_content:
١١٠٨٧ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إذا أراد أحدكم أمرًا فليقل: اللهم إني أستخيرك بعلمك، وأستقدرك بقدرتك، وأسألك من فضلك العظيم؛ فإنك تقدر ولا أقدر، وتعلم ولا أعلم، وأنت علام الغيوب.
اللهم إن كان كذا وكذا خيرًا لي في ديني، وخيرًا لي في معيشتي، وخيرًا لي في عاقبة أمري، فاقدره لي، وبارك لي فيه. وإن كان غير ذلك خيرًا لي، فاقدر لي الخير حيثما كان، ورضني بقدرك)).
حسن: رواه ابن حبان (٨٨٦)، والبخاري في التاريخ (٤/٢٥٨)، والطبراني في الدعاء (١٣٠٦).
11087 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When one of you intends to undertake a matter, let him say: ‘O Allah, I seek the better choice through Your knowledge, and I seek ability through Your power. I ask You from Your immense bounty, for You are able while I am not, You know while I do not, and You are the Knower of all unseen things.
O Allah, if such-and-such a matter is good for me in my religion, good for me in my livelihood, and good for me in the final outcome of my affair, then decree it for me and bless it for me. If something else is better for me, then decree good for me wherever it may be and make me content with Your decree.’”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān (886), al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh (4/258), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ (1306).

وزاد في رواية: ((فتبارك اللّٰه أحسن الخالقين)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٥٨٠)، والنسائي (١١٢٩)، والحاكم (١/٢٢٠).

١١٠٨٩ — عن ابن عباس أن النبي ﷺ دخل على أعرابي يعوده. قال: وكان النبي ﷺ إذا دخل على مريض يعوده قال له: ((لا بأس، طهور إن شاء اللّٰه)).
قال: قلت: طهور؟ كلا، بل هي حمى تفور - أو تثور - على شيخ كبير، تزيره القبور. فقال النبي ﷺ: ((فنعم إذًا)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٦٥٦).
قوله: «تزيره»، من أزاره إذا حمله على الزيارة بغير اختياره.

11089 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ entered upon a Bedouin to visit him during his illness.
Whenever the Prophet ﷺ visited a sick person, he would say:
“There is no harm. It is a purification, Allah willing.”
The Bedouin replied:
“A purification? No! Rather, it is a fever boiling—or raging—upon an elderly man, causing him to visit the graves.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Then so it shall be.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5656).
The expression “causing him to visit” means compelling him to make the visit without his choosing it.

11090 — Anas narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon a Bedouin to visit him while he was suffering from fever.
He said:
“It is an expiation and a purification.”
The Bedouin replied:
“Rather, it is a fever boiling upon an elderly man, causing him to visit the graves.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then stood and left him.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (13616).

١١٠٩١ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو بن العاص قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إذا جاء الرجل يعود مريضًا فليقل: اللهم اشف عبدك، ينكأ لك عدوًا، أو يمشي لك إلى جنازة)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣١٠٧)، وصححه ابن حبان (٢٩٧٤)، والحاكم (١/٣٤٤، ٥٤٩).
وقوله: ((ينكأ))، أي: يكثر فيهم الجرح والقتل.

11091 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When a man visits a sick person, let him say: ‘O Allah, heal Your servant, so that he may wound an enemy for Your sake or walk in a funeral procession for Your sake.’”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3107), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (2974) and al-Ḥākim (1/344, 549).
The word yankaʾ means to inflict extensive wounds and losses upon the enemy.

١١٠٩٢ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((لقنوا موتاكم: لا إله إلا اللّٰه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩١٦).
قوله: ((لقنوا موتاكم))، المراد: من حضره الموت، لا من مات. والمقصود من هذا التلقين أن يكون آخر كلامه: لا إله إلا اللّٰه.

11092 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Prompt your dying people to say: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (916).
The words “your dying people” refer to those who are approaching death, not those who have already died. The purpose of prompting them is so that their final words may be:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.”

١١٠٩٦ — عن أنس أن النبي ﷺ دخل على رجل من بني النجار يعوده، فقال له رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((يا خال، قل: لا إله إلا اللّٰه)). فقال: أوخال أنا، أو عم؟ فقال النبي ﷺ: ((لا، بل خال)). فقال له: ((قل: لا إله إلا هو)). قال: خير لي؟ قال: ((نعم)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٢٥٤٣، ١٢٥٦٣، ١٣٨٢٦)، والبزار في كشف الأستار (٧٨٧)، وأبو يعلى (٣٥١٢).

11096 — Anas narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ entered upon a man from Banū al-Najjār to visit him during his illness.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him:
“O maternal uncle, say: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah.’”
The man asked:
“Am I your maternal uncle or your paternal uncle?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“No, rather, you are my maternal uncle.”
He then said to him:
“Say: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Him.’”
The man asked:
“Is that better for me?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (12543, 12563, 13826), al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (787), and Abū Yaʿlā (3512).

١١٠٩٨ — عن الأغر أبي مسلم قال: أشهد على أبي سعيد وأبي هريرة أنهما شهدا على النبي ﷺ أنه قال: ((من قال: لا إله إلا اللّٰه، واللّٰه أكبر، صدقه ربه فقال: لا إله إلا أنا، وأنا أكبر. وإذا قال: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده، قال: يقول اللّٰه: لا إله إلا أنا وحدي. وإذا قال: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، قال اللّٰه: لا إله إلا أنا وحدي لا شريك لي. وإذا قال: لا إله إلا اللّٰه، له الملك وله الحمد، قال اللّٰه: لا إله إلا أنا، لي الملك ولي الحمد. وإذا قال: لا إله إلا اللّٰه، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا باللّٰه، قال اللّٰه: لا إله إلا أنا، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بي)).
وكان يقول: ((من قالها في مرضه ثم مات لم تطعمه النار)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٣٤٣٠)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٣٠)، وابن ماجه (٣٧٩٤)، والنسائي (٣١)، وصححه ابن حبان (٨٥١)، والحاكم (١/٥)، ورواه النسائي أيضًا (٣٤٨).

11098 — Al-Agharr Abū Muslim said:
I bear witness concerning Abū Saʿīd and Abū Hurayrah that they both bore witness that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever says, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest,’ his Lord confirms him and says: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Me, and I am the Greatest.’
When he says, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone,’ Allah says: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Me alone.’
When he says, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner,’ Allah says: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Me alone, and I have no partner.’
When he says, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah; to Him belong all sovereignty and all praise,’ Allah says: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Me; to Me belong all sovereignty and all praise.’
When he says, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and there is no power and no strength except through Allah,’ Allah says: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Me, and there is no power and no strength except through Me.’”
The Prophet ﷺ would also say:
“Whoever says these words during his illness and then dies, the Fire will not consume him.”

١١٠٩٩ — عن أم سلمة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت: دخل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ على أبي سلمة، وقد شق بصره، فأغمضه، ثم قال: ((إن الروح إذا قبض تبعه البصر)). فضج ناس من أهله، فقال: ((لا تدعوا على أنفسكم إلا بخير؛ فإن الملائكة يؤمنون على ما تقولون)).
ثم قال: ((اللهم اغفر لأبي سلمة، وارفع درجته في المهديين، واخلفه في عقبه في الغابرين، واغفر لنا وله يا رب العالمين، وافسح له في قبره، ونور له فيه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩٢٠).

11099 — Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Abū Salamah after his eyes had become fixed open. He closed them and then said:
“When the soul is taken, the sight follows it.”
Some members of his family began crying out loudly.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Do not supplicate against yourselves except with good words, for the angels say ‘Āmīn’ to whatever you say.”
He then said:
“O Allah, forgive Abū Salamah, raise his rank among the rightly guided, and take care of those he has left behind among those who remain. Forgive us and him, O Lord of the worlds. Make his grave spacious for him and illuminate it for him.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (920).

11100 — Umm Salamah narrated:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“No Muslim is afflicted by a calamity and then says what Allah has commanded: ‘Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed, to Him we shall return. O Allah, reward me for my calamity and replace it for me with something better,’ except that Allah replaces it for him with something better.”
She said:
When Abū Salamah died, I said:
“Which Muslim could be better than Abū Salamah, the first household to migrate to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?”
Nevertheless, I said the supplication, and Allah replaced him for me with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
She said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah to propose marriage to me on his behalf. I said:
“I have a daughter, and I am intensely jealous.”
He said:
“As for her daughter, we shall supplicate to Allah to make her independent of her, and I shall supplicate to Allah to remove her jealousy.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (918).

11101 — Umm Salamah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When you are present with a sick or deceased person, say only good things, for the angels say ‘Āmīn’ to whatever you say.”
She said:
When Abū Salamah died, I went to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Abū Salamah has died.”
He said:
“Say: ‘O Allah, forgive me and him, and grant me a good successor after him.’”

11102 — Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated:
We were with the Prophet ﷺ when a messenger from one of his daughters came, asking him to come because her son was dying.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Return to her and tell her that to Allah belongs whatever He takes and whatever He gives, and everything with Him has an appointed term. Therefore, instruct her to remain patient and seek the reward from Allah.”
She sent the messenger back, saying that she had sworn that he must come to her.
The Prophet ﷺ then stood, accompanied by Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah and Muʿādh ibn Jabal. The child was placed in his arms while his breathing rattled like water inside an old leather water-skin. The eyes of the Prophet ﷺ overflowed with tears.
Saʿd asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what is this?”
He replied:
“This is mercy which Allah has placed within the hearts of His servants. Allah shows mercy only to those of His servants who are merciful.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7377) and Muslim (923).

١١١٠٣ — عن عوف بن مالك قال: صلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ على جنازة، فحفظت من دعائه، وهو يقول: ((اللهم اغفر له وارحمه، وعافه واعف عنه، وأكرم نزله، ووسع مدخله، واغسله بالماء والثلج والبرد، ونقه من الخطايا كما نقيت الثوب الأبيض من الدنس، وأبدله دارًا خيرًا من داره، وأهلًا خيرًا من أهله، وزوجًا خيرًا من زوجه، وأدخله الجنة، وأعذه من عذاب القبر - أو من عذاب النار)).
قال: حتى تمنيت أن أكون أنا ذلك الميت.
وفي لفظ: ((كما ينقى الثوب الأبيض)) بدل: ((كما نقيت الثوب الأبيض)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩٦٣).

11103 — ʿAwf ibn Mālik narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the funeral prayer over a deceased person, and I memorized the following from his supplication:
“O Allah, forgive him and have mercy upon him. Grant him well-being and pardon him. Honor his reception and make his entrance spacious. Wash him with water, snow, and hail. Purify him of sins as You have purified a white garment from filth.
Replace his home with a better home, his family with a better family, and his spouse with a better spouse. Admit him into Paradise and protect him from the punishment of the grave—or from the punishment of the Fire.”
ʿAwf said:
“I wished that I had been that deceased person.”
Another wording states:
“As a white garment is purified,”
instead of:
“As You purified a white garment.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (963).

11104 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the funeral prayer over a deceased person and said:
“O Allah, forgive our living and our dead, our young and our old, our males and our females, those of us who are present and those who are absent.
O Allah, whoever among us You keep alive, keep him alive upon faith, and whoever among us You cause to die, cause him to die upon Islam. O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward and do not lead us astray after him.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3201), al-Tirmidhī (1024), and Ibn Mājah (1498), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (3070) and al-Ḥākim (1/358).

١١١٠٧ — عن واثلة بن الأسقع قال: صلى بنا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ على رجل من المسلمين، فسمعته يقول: ((اللهم إن فلان بن فلان في ذمتك، وحبل جوارك، فقه من فتنة القبر وعذاب النار، وأنت أهل الوفاء والحق - وفي رواية: الحمد - اللهم فاغفر له وارحمه، إنك أنت الغفور الرحيم)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٢٠٢)، وابن ماجه (١٤٩٩)، وأحمد (١٦٠١٨)، وصححه ابن حبان (٣٠٧٤).
وقوله: ((حبل جوارك))، قال بعضهم: كان من عادة العرب أن يخيف بعضهم بعضًا، فكان الرجل إذا أراد سفرًا أخذ عهدًا من سيد كل قبيلة، فيأمن به ما دام في حدودها، حتى ينتهي إلى الأخرى فيأخذ مثل ذلك. فهذا حبل الجوار، أي: ما دام مجاورًا أرضه. أو هو من الإجارة، وهي الأمان والنصرة. قاله المنذري.

11107 — Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the funeral prayer over a Muslim man, and I heard him say:
“O Allah, so-and-so, the son of so-and-so, is under Your protection and the covenant of Your security. Protect him from the trial of the grave and the punishment of the Fire. You are worthy of fulfilling promises and establishing the truth.”
Another narration states:
“You are worthy of all praise.”
He continued:
“O Allah, forgive him and have mercy upon him. Indeed, You are the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3202), Ibn Mājah (1499), and Aḥmad (16018), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (3074).
Regarding the phrase “the covenant of Your protection,” some scholars explained that the Arabs would sometimes threaten one another. When a man intended to travel, he would obtain a pledge of protection from the leader of each tribe. He would remain safe within that tribe’s territory until reaching the next tribe, from whose leader he would obtain a similar pledge.
This was called the covenant of protection, meaning that a person remained secure while residing within that territory. It may also be derived from ijārah, meaning protection, security, and assistance. This explanation was mentioned by al-Mundhirī.

١١١٠٩ — عن ابن عمر أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا وضع الميت في القبر قال: ((بسم اللّٰه، وعلى سنة رسول اللّٰه)).
وفي رواية: ((وعلى ملة رسول اللّٰه)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٣٢١٣)، وأحمد (٤٨١٢)، والنسائي في السنن الكبرى (١٠٩٢٧)، وصححه ابن حبان (٣١١٠)، والحاكم (١/٣٦٦).
11109 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated:
When the Prophet ﷺ placed the deceased in the grave, he would say:
“In the name of Allah and upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah.”
Another narration states:
“And upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3213), Aḥmad (4812), and al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (10927), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (3110) and al-Ḥākim (1/366).

حسن: أخرجه أبو داود (٣٢٢١).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩٧٤).

“Peace be upon you, dwelling place of believing people. What you were promised has come to you. You have been granted respite until tomorrow, and we, if Allah wills, will join you. O Allah, forgive the inhabitants of Baqīʿ al-Gharqad.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (974).

arabic_source:
١١١١٢ — عن عائشة قالت: قلت: كيف أقول لهم - تعني أهل البقيع - يا رسول اللّٰه؟ قال: ((قولي: السلام على أهل الديار من المؤمنين والمسلمين، ويرحم اللّٰه المستقدمين منا والمستأخرين، وإنا إن شاء اللّٰه بكم للاحقون)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩٧٤).

11112 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
I asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what should I say to them?”
She meant the inhabitants of al-Baqīʿ.
He replied:
“Say: ‘Peace be upon the inhabitants of these dwellings from among the believers and Muslims. May Allah have mercy upon those of us who have gone ahead and those who will come later. We, if Allah wills, will surely join you.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (974).

١١١١٣ — عن بريدة بن الحصيب قال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يعلمهم إذا خرجوا إلى المقابر، فكان قائلهم يقول - في رواية أبي بكر -: ((السلام على أهل الديار)). وفي رواية زهير: ((السلام عليكم أهل الديار من المؤمنين والمسلمين، وإنا إن شاء اللّٰه للاحقون، أسأل اللّٰه لنا ولكم العافية)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٩٧٥).
وزاد النسائي (٢٠٤٠) بعد قوله: ((بكم لاحقون)): ((أنتم لنا فرط، ونحن لكم تبع، أسأل اللّٰه العافية لنا ولكم)).

english_source:
11113 — Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would teach them what to say when they went out to the graveyards.
In Abū Bakr’s narration, the speaker would say:
“Peace be upon the inhabitants of these dwellings.”
In Zuhayr’s narration, he would say:
“Peace be upon you, inhabitants of these dwellings, from among the believers and Muslims. We, if Allah wills, will join you. I ask Allah to grant well-being to us and to you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (975).
Al-Nasāʾī (2040) added after the words “we will join you”:
“You have gone ahead of us, and we will follow you. I ask Allah to grant well-being to us and to you.”

١١١١٧ — عن وائل بن حجر أن النبي ﷺ بعث ساعيًا، فأتى رجلًا، فأتاه فصيلًا مخلولًا. فقال النبي ﷺ: ((بعثنا مصدق اللّٰه ورسوله، وإن فلانًا أعطاه فصيلًا مخلولًا! اللهم لا تبارك فيه، ولا في إبله)).
فبلغ ذلك الرجل، فجاء بناقة حسناء، فقال: أتوب إلى اللّٰه عز وجل وإلى نبيه ﷺ. فقال النبي ﷺ: ((اللهم بارك فيه وفي إبله)).
حسن: رواه النسائي (٢٤٥٨)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (٢٢٧٤).

11117 — Wāʾil ibn Ḥujr narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ sent a charity collector. When the collector went to a man, the man gave him a weak young camel.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“We sent the collector of Allah and His Messenger, yet so-and-so gave him a weak young camel! O Allah, do not bless him or his camels.”
When the man heard about this, he came with a fine she-camel and said:
“I repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to His Prophet ﷺ.”
The Prophet ﷺ then said:
“O Allah, bless him and his camels.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (2458), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (2274).

١١١١٨ — عن مروان - يعني ابن سالم المقنع - قال: رأيت ابن عمر يقبض على لحيته، فيقطع ما زاد على الكف، وقال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إذا أفطر قال: ((ذهب الظمأ، وابتلت العروق، وثبت الأجر إن شاء اللّٰه)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٣٥٧)، والنسائي في السنن الكبرى (٣٣١٥)، والدارقطني (٢٢٧٩)، والحاكم (١/٤٢٢)، والبيهقي (٤/٢٣٩).

11118 — Marwān—meaning Ibn Sālim al-Muqannaʿ—narrated:
I saw Ibn ʿUmar grasp his beard and cut whatever extended beyond a fistful.
He said:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ broke his fast, he would say:
“The thirst has gone, the veins have been moistened, and the reward has been confirmed, if Allah wills.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2357), al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (3315), al-Dāraquṭnī (2279), al-Ḥākim (1/422), and al-Bayhaqī (4/239).

١١١١٩ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إذا أفطر عند قوم دعا لهم، فقال: ((أفطر عندكم الصائمون، وأكل طعامكم الأبرار، وصلت عليكم الملائكة)).
حسن: رواه ابن السني في عمل اليوم والليلة (٤٨٢)، والطبراني في الدعاء (٩٢٥).

11119 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ broke his fast with a group of people, he would supplicate for them, saying:
“May those who fast break their fast with you, may the righteous eat your food, and may the angels invoke blessings upon you.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn al-Sunnī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (482) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ (925).

١١١٢٠ — عن عائشة قالت: قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، أرأيت إن علمت ليلة القدر، ما أقول فيها؟ قال: ((قولي: اللهم إنك عفو تحب العفو، فاعف عني)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٣٥١٣)، وابن ماجه (٣٨٥٠)، وأحمد (٢٥٣٨٤)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٨٧٢، ٨٧٣، ٨٧٤)، والحاكم (١/٥٣٠)، والبيهقي في فضائل الأوقات (١١٣).

11120 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
I asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, if I know which night is Laylat al-Qadr, what should I say during it?”
He replied:
“Say: ‘O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love to pardon, so pardon me.’”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3513), Ibn Mājah (3850), Aḥmad (25384), al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (872, 873, 874), al-Ḥākim (1/530), and al-Bayhaqī in Faḍāʾil al-Awqāt (113).

١١١٢١ — عن أنس قال: صلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ونحن معه بالمدينة الظهر أربعًا، والعصر بذي الحليفة ركعتين، ثم بات بها حتى أصبح، ثم ركب حتى استوت به على البيداء، حمد اللّٰه وسبح وكبر، ثم أهل بحج وعمرة، وأهل الناس بهما. فلما قدمنا أمر الناس فحلوا، حتى كان يوم التروية أهلوا بالحج. قال: ونحر النبي ﷺ بدنات بيده قيامًا، وذبح رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بالمدينة كبشين أملحين.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٥٥١)، ومسلم (٦٩٠).

11121 — Anas narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed four units of Ẓuhr with us in Madinah and two units of ʿAṣr at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah. He then spent the night there until morning.
Afterward, he mounted his riding animal. When it stood upright with him upon al-Bayḍāʾ, he praised Allah, glorified Him, and proclaimed His greatness. He then entered the state of iḥrām for both Ḥajj and ʿUmrah, and the people also entered iḥrām for both.
When we arrived, he instructed the people to leave the state of iḥrām. Then, when the Day of Tarwiyah came, they entered iḥrām for Ḥajj.
Anas said:
The Prophet ﷺ slaughtered sacrificial camels with his own hand while they were standing, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also slaughtered two predominantly white rams with black markings in Madinah.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1551) and Muslim (690).

١١١٢٢ — عن ابن عمر أن تلبية رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كانت: ((لبيك اللهم لبيك، لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك، إن الحمد والنعمة لك والملك، لا شريك لك)).
قال: وكان عبد اللّٰه بن عمر يزيد فيها: لبيك لبيك، لبيك وسعديك، والخير بيديك، لبيك والرغباء إليك والعمل.
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٢٨)، والبخاري (١٥٤٩)، ومسلم (١١٨٤/١٩).

11122 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the talbiyah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was:
“Here I am at Your service, O Allah, here I am. Here I am at Your service; You have no partner, here I am. Indeed, all praise, every blessing, and all sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner.”
ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar would add:
“Here I am at Your service, here I am. Here I am in obedience and happiness. All goodness is in Your hands. Here I am at Your service; all desire and all deeds are directed toward You.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik (28), al-Bukhārī (1549), and Muslim (1184/19).
