11215 — Juwayriyyah, the Mother of the Believers, narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ left her early in the morning after performing the Fajr prayer while she remained in her place of prayer. He returned after the morning had advanced and found her still sitting there.
He asked:
“Have you remained in the same state in which I left you?”
She replied:
“Yes.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“After leaving you, I said four phrases three times. Were they to be weighed against everything you have said since the beginning of the day, they would outweigh it: ‘Glory be to Allah and all praise belongs to Him, by the number of His creation, in accordance with His pleasure, by the weight of His Throne, and by the extent of the ink of His words.’”
Another narration states:
“Glory be to Allah by the number of His creation. Glory be to Allah in accordance with His pleasure. Glory be to Allah by the weight of His Throne. Glory be to Allah by the extent of the ink of His words.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2726/79).

١١٢١٦ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن مسعود قال: كان نبي اللّٰه ﷺ إذا أمسى قال: ((أمسينا وأمسى الملك للّٰه، والحمد للّٰه، لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له)). قال: أراه قال فيهن: ((له الملك وله الحمد، وهو على كل شيء قدير. رب، أسألك خير ما في هذه الليلة، وخير ما بعدها، وأعوذ بك من شر ما في هذه الليلة، وشر ما بعدها. رب، أعوذ بك من الكسل، وسوء الكبر. رب، أعوذ بك من عذاب في النار، وعذاب في القبر)).
وإذا أصبح قال ذلك أيضًا: ((أصبحنا وأصبح الملك للّٰه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٧٢٣/٧٥).

11216 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated:
When evening came, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ would say:
“We have entered the evening, and all sovereignty has entered the evening belonging to Allah. All praise belongs to Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner.”
The narrator said:
I believe he also said:
“To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good contained within this night and the good that follows it. I seek refuge in You from the evil contained within this night and the evil that follows it.
My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the evils of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.”
When morning came, he would say the same, beginning with:
“We have entered the morning, and all sovereignty has entered the morning belonging to Allah.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2723/75).

١١٢١٧ — عن شداد بن أوس، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((سيد الاستغفار أن تقول: اللهم أنت ربي، لا إله إلا أنت، خلقتني وأنا عبدك، وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت، أعوذ بك من شر ما صنعت، أبوء لك بنعمتك علي، وأبوء لك بذنبي، فاغفر لي؛ فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت)).
قال: ((ومن قالها من النهار موقنًا بها، فمات من يومه قبل أن يمسي، فهو من أهل الجنة. ومن قالها من الليل وهو موقن بها، فمات قبل أن يصبح، فهو من أهل الجنة)).
وفي لفظ: ((إذا قال حين يمسي فمات، دخل الجنة، أو كان من أهل الجنة. وإذا قال حين يصبح فمات من يومه، مثله)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٣٢٣، ٦٣٠٦).

11217 — Shaddād ibn Aws narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“The supreme supplication for seeking forgiveness is to say: ‘O Allah, You are my Lord. There is no deity worthy of worship except You. You created me, and I am Your servant. I remain faithful to Your covenant and promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge before You Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.’”
He said:
“Whoever says it during the day with certainty in it and dies that day before evening will be among the people of Paradise. Whoever says it during the night with certainty in it and dies before morning will be among the people of Paradise.”
Another wording states:
“If he says it in the evening and then dies, he will enter Paradise—or he will be among the people of Paradise. If he says it in the morning and dies during that day, the same applies to him.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6323, 6306).

11218 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever says one hundred times in the morning and one hundred times in the evening, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things,’ no one will bring anything better than what he has brought, except someone who did something superior to that.”
Another wording states:
“Whoever says two hundred times each day, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things,’ no one before him will have surpassed him, and no one after him will catch up with him, except someone whose deeds were better.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (575) and Ibn al-Sunnī (76) with the first wording. The second wording was narrated by Aḥmad (6740) and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (577).
The words “two hundred times” are an abbreviated expression explained by the first narration: one hundred times in the morning and one hundred times in the evening.

To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things,’ no one will bring anything better than what he has brought, except someone who did something superior to that.”
Another wording states:
“Whoever says two hundred times each day, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things,’ no one before him will have surpassed him, and no one after him will catch up with him, except someone whose deeds were better.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (575) and Ibn al-Sunnī (76) with the first wording. The second wording was narrated by Aḥmad (6740) and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (577).
The words “two hundred times” are an abbreviated expression explained by the first narration: one hundred times in the morning and one hundred times in the evening.

١١٢٢٠ — عن أبي عياش الزرقي قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((من قال إذا أصبح: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، وهو على كل شيء قدير، كان له عدل رقبة من ولد إسماعيل، وكتب له عشر حسنات، وحط عنه عشر سيئات، ورفع له عشر درجات، وكان في حرز من الشيطان حتى يمسي. وإن قالها إذا أمسى، كان له مثل ذلك حتى يصبح)).
قال: فرأى رجل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فيما يرى النائم فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، إن أبا عياش يحدث عنك بكذا وكذا. قال: ((صدق أبو عياش)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٧٧)، وابن ماجه (٣٨٦٧)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٢٧)، وأحمد (١٦٥٨٣).

11220 — Abū ʿAyyāsh al-Zuraqī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever says in the morning, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things,’ will receive a reward equivalent to freeing a slave from the descendants of Ishmael. Ten good deeds will be recorded for him, ten sins will be erased from him, he will be raised ten ranks, and he will be protected from Satan until evening.
If he says it in the evening, he will receive the same until morning.”
A man later saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a dream and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Abū ʿAyyāsh narrates such-and-such from you.”
He replied:
“Abū ʿAyyāsh has spoken the truth.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5077), Ibn Mājah (3867), al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (27), and Aḥmad (16583).

١١٢٢١ — عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري، عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال: ((من قال حين يصبح: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، يحيي ويميت، وهو على كل شيء قدير، عشر مرات، كتب اللّٰه له بكل واحدة قالها عشر حسنات، وحط اللّٰه عنه بها عشر سيئات، ورفعه اللّٰه بها عشر درجات، وكن له كعشر رقاب، وكن له مسلحة من أول النهار إلى آخره، ولم يعمل يومئذ عملًا يقهرهن. فإن قال حين يمسي، فمثل ذلك)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣٥٦٨)، والطبراني في الكبير (٤/١٥١).

11221 — Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever says ten times in the morning, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise. He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things,’ Allah will record ten good deeds for every time he says it, erase ten sins through it, and raise him ten ranks.
The ten repetitions will be equivalent to freeing ten slaves, and they will serve as an armed guard for him from the beginning of the day until its end. He will perform no deed that day capable of surpassing them. If he says the same in the evening, he will receive the same.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (23568) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (4/151).

Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (23568) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (4/151).

١١٢٢٣ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عبد الرحمن بن أبزى، عن أبيه، عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إذا أصبح يقول: ((أصبحنا على فطرة الإسلام، وكلمة الإخلاص، ودين نبينا محمد ﷺ، وعلى ملة أبينا إبراهيم حنيفًا مسلمًا، وما كان من المشركين)).

١١٢٢٤ — عن ابن عمر قال: لم يكن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يدع هؤلاء الدعوات حين يمسي وحين يصبح: ((اللهم إني أسألك العافية في الدنيا والآخرة. اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية في ديني ودنياي وأهلي ومالي. اللهم استر عوراتي، وآمن روعاتي. اللهم احفظني من بين يدي، ومن خلفي، وعن يميني، وعن شمالي، ومن فوقي، وأعوذ بعظمتك أن أغتال من تحتي)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٧٤)، والنسائي (٥٥٢٩)، وابن ماجه (٣٨٧١)، وأحمد (٤٧٨٥)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (١٢٠٠)، وصححه ابن حبان (٩٦١)، والحاكم (١/٥١٧-٥١٨).

english_source:
11224 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never neglected these supplications in the evening and the morning:
“O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly affairs, my family, and my wealth.
O Allah, conceal my faults and grant me security from my fears. O Allah, protect me from in front of me, from behind me, from my right, from my left, and from above me. I seek refuge in Your greatness from being suddenly destroyed from beneath me.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5074), al-Nasāʾī (5529), Ibn Mājah (3871), Aḥmad (4785), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (1200), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (961) and al-Ḥākim (1/517–518).

١١٢٢٥ — عن أبان بن عثمان قال: سمعت عثمان بن عفان يقول: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((ما من عبد يقول في صباح كل يوم ومساء كل ليلة: بسم اللّٰه الذي لا يضر مع اسمه شيء في الأرض ولا في السماء، وهو السميع العليم، ثلاث مرات، فيضره شيء)).
وكان أبان قد أصابه طرف فالج، فجعل الرجل ينظر إليه، فقال له أبان: ما تنظر؟ أما إن الحديث كما حدثتك، ولكني لم أقله يومئذ ليمضي اللّٰه علي قدره.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٨٨، ٥٠٨٩)، والترمذي (٣٣٨٨)، وابن ماجه (٣٨٦٩)، وأحمد (٤٤٦)، وصححه ابن حبان (٨٥٢، ٨٦٢)، والحاكم (١/٥١٤).

11225 — Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated:
I heard ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“No servant says three times every morning and every evening, ‘In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,’ and then suffers harm.”
Abān had been afflicted with partial paralysis. A man began looking at him, so Abān said:
“Why are you looking at me? The hadith is exactly as I narrated it to you. However, I did not say it on that particular day so that Allah’s decree concerning me might be carried out.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5088, 5089), al-Tirmidhī (3388), Ibn Mājah (3869), Aḥmad (446), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (852, 862) and al-Ḥākim (1/514).

صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٨٨، ٥٠٨٩)، والترمذي (٣٣٨٨)، وابن ماجه (٣٨٦٩)، وأحمد (٤٤٦)، وصححه ابن حبان (٨٥٢، ٨٦٢)، والحاكم (١/٥١٤).
11225 — Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated:
I heard ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“No servant says three times every morning and every evening, ‘In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,’ and then suffers harm.”
Abān had been afflicted with partial paralysis. A man began looking at him, so Abān said:
“Why are you looking at me? The hadith is exactly as I narrated it to you. However, I did not say it on that particular day so that Allah’s decree concerning me might be carried out.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5088, 5089), al-Tirmidhī (3388), Ibn Mājah (3869), Aḥmad (446), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (852, 862) and al-Ḥākim (1/514).

١١٢٢٦ — عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة أنه قال لأبيه: يا أبت، إني أسمعك تدعو كل غداة: ((اللهم عافني في بدني، اللهم عافني في سمعي، اللهم عافني في بصري، لا إله إلا أنت)). تعيدها ثلاثًا حين تصبح، وثلاثًا حين تمسي.

قال: وقال النبي ﷺ: ((دعوات المكروب: اللهم رحمتك أرجو، فلا تكلني إلى نفسي طرفة عين، وأصلح لي شأني كله، لا إله إلا أنت)).

11226 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakrah said to his father:
“My father, I hear you supplicate every morning:
‘O Allah, grant well-being to my body. O Allah, grant well-being to my hearing. O Allah, grant well-being to my sight. There is no deity worthy of worship except You.’
You repeat it three times in the morning and three times in the evening.
You also say:
‘O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave. There is no deity worthy of worship except You.’
You repeat this three times in the morning and three times in the evening.”
He replied:
“Yes, my son. I heard the Prophet ﷺ supplicate with these words, and I wish to follow his Sunnah.”
He also narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“The supplications of a person in distress are: ‘O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for, so do not leave me in charge of myself even for the blink of an eye. Set right all of my affairs. There is no deity worthy of worship except You.’”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5090), Aḥmad (20430), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (701), and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (22, 572, 651); authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (970) with only the supplication for distress. The wording cited here is that of Aḥmad and al-Bukhārī.

11227 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ said to Fāṭimah:
“What prevents you from listening to what I advise you to say? Say in the morning and in the evening: ‘O Ever-Living, O Sustainer of all, I seek relief through Your mercy. Set right all of my affairs and do not leave me in charge of myself even for the blink of an eye.’”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (570), al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (3107), Ibn al-Sunnī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (49), and al-Ḥākim (1/545).

١١٢٢٨ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: ((من قال: رضيت باللّٰه ربًا، وبالإسلام دينًا، وبمحمد رسولًا، وجبت له الجنة)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٥٢٩)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٥)، وصححه ابن حبان (٨٦٣)، والحاكم (١/٥١٨).
ورواه مسلم (١٨٨٤) من طريق آخر، عن أبي سعيد الخدري، أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: ((يا أبا سعيد، من رضي باللّٰه ربًا، وبالإسلام دينًا، وبمحمد نبيًا، وجبت له الجنة)). فعجب لها أبو سعيد فقال: أعدها علي يا رسول اللّٰه. ففعل. ثم قال: ((وأخرى يرفع بها العبد مائة درجة في الجنة، ما بين كل درجتين كما بين السماء والأرض)). قال: وما هي يا رسول اللّٰه؟ قال: ((الجهاد في سبيل اللّٰه، الجهاد في سبيل اللّٰه)).
ولا منافاة بين اللفظين، فإن معناه: من قال بلسانه وهو راض بقلبه. ويدل على ذلك ما رواه الإمام أحمد (١١١٠٢) بسنده عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: أخذ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بيدي فقال: ((يا أبا سعيد، ثلاثة من قالهن دخل الجنة)). قلت: ما هن يا رسول اللّٰه؟ قال: ((من رضي باللّٰه ربًا، وبالإسلام دينًا، وبمحمد رسولًا)). ثم قال: ((يا أبا سعيد، والرابعة لها من الفضل كما بين السماء إلى الأرض، وهي: الجهاد في سبيل اللّٰه)).

11228 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever says, ‘I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islam as my religion, and with Muḥammad as my Messenger,’ Paradise becomes obligatory for him.”

“O Abū Saʿīd, whoever is pleased with Allah as his Lord, with Islam as his religion, and with Muḥammad as his Prophet, Paradise becomes obligatory for him.”

“Repeat them to me, O Messenger of Allah.”
He repeated them and then said:
“There is another deed by which a servant is raised one hundred ranks in Paradise, the distance between every two ranks being like the distance between heaven and earth.”
He asked:
“What is it, O Messenger of Allah?”
He replied:
“Jihād in the path of Allah. Jihād in the path of Allah.”

“Whoever is pleased with Allah as his Lord, with Islam as his religion, and with Muḥammad as his Messenger.”
He then said:
“O Abū Saʿīd, the fourth has a superiority as vast as the distance between heaven and earth: jihād in the path of Allah.”

١١٢٢٩ — عن أبي سلام قال: مر رجل في مسجد حمص، فقالوا: هذا خدم النبي ﷺ. قال: فقمت إليه، فقلت: حدثني حديثًا سمعته من رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، لا يتداوله بينك وبينه الرجال. قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((ما من عبد مسلم يقول حين يصبح وحين يمسي ثلاث مرات: رضيت باللّٰه ربًا، وبالإسلام دينًا، وبمحمد نبيًا، إلا كان حقًا على اللّٰه أن يرضيه يوم القيامة)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٧٢)، وأحمد (١٨٩٦٧، ١٨٩٦٩)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٤).

11229 — Abū Salām narrated:
A man passed through the mosque of Ḥimṣ, and the people said:
“This man served the Prophet ﷺ.”
I went to him and said:
“Narrate to me a hadith that you personally heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, without any men transmitting it between you and him.”
He said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“No Muslim servant says three times in the morning and three times in the evening, ‘I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islam as my religion, and with Muḥammad as my Prophet,’ except that Allah has undertaken to please him on the Day of Resurrection.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5072), Aḥmad (18967, 18969), and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (4).

11230 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Khubayb narrated:
We were overtaken by light rain and darkness, so we waited for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to come and lead us in prayer.
He came out, took hold of my hand, and said:
“Recite.”
I remained silent.
He said again:
“Recite.”
I asked:
“What should I recite?”
He replied:
“Recite ‘Say: He is Allah, the One,’ and the two sūrahs of seeking refuge three times in the evening and three times in the morning. They will suffice you against everything.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5082), al-Tirmidhī (3575), al-Nasāʾī (5428), and Aḥmad (22664).

١١٢٣٠ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن خبيب قال: أصابنا طش وظلمة، فانتظرنا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ليصلي لنا. فخرج، فأخذ بيدي فقال: ((قل)). فسكت. قال: ((قل)). قلت: ما أقول؟ قال: ((قل هو اللّٰه أحد، والمعوذتين حين تمسي، وحين تصبح ثلاثًا، تكفيك من كل شيء)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٨٢)، والترمذي (٣٥٧٥)، والنسائي (٥٤٢٨)، وأحمد (٢٢٦٦٤).
11230 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Khubayb narrated:
We were overtaken by light rain and darkness, so we waited for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to come and lead us in prayer.
He came out, took hold of my hand, and said:
“Recite.”
I remained silent.
He said again:
“Recite.”
I asked:
“What should I recite?”
He replied:
“Recite ‘Say: He is Allah, the One,’ and the two sūrahs of seeking refuge three times in the evening and three times in the morning. They will suffice you against everything.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5082), al-Tirmidhī (3575), al-Nasāʾī (5428), and Aḥmad (22664).

english_source:
11231 — Ubayy ibn Kaʿb had a storage area containing dates, but the dates were continually decreasing. One night, he guarded it and saw a creature resembling a boy who had reached puberty.
Ubayy greeted him, and he returned the greeting.
Ubayy asked:
“What are you—a jinn or a human being?”
He replied:
“No, I am a jinn.”
Ubayy said:
“Give me your hand.”
The creature extended its hand. Its hand was like the paw of a dog, and its hair was like the hair of a dog.
Ubayy asked:
“Is this how the jinn were created?”
He replied:
“The jinn know that there is no man among them stronger than I am.”
Ubayy asked:
“What brought you here?”
He replied:
“We heard that you love charity, so we came to take some of your food.”
Ubayy asked:
“What protects us from you?”
He replied:
“This verse in Sūrat al-Baqarah:
‘Allah—there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all.’
Whoever recites it in the evening will be protected from us until morning, and whoever recites it in the morning will be protected from us until evening.”
When morning came, Ubayy went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him of what had happened.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“The wicked one spoke the truth.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr (1/27) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (1/169).

١١٢٣٢ — عن البراء بن عازب قال: قال لي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((إذا أتيت مضجعك، فتوضأ وضوءك للصلاة، ثم اضطجع على شقك الأيمن، وقل: اللهم أسلمت نفسي إليك، وفوضت أمري إليك، وألجأت ظهري إليك، رهبة ورغبة إليك، لا ملجأ ولا منجى منك إلا إليك، آمنت بكتابك الذي أنزلت، وبنبيك الذي أرسلت، فإن مت مت على الفطرة، فاجعلهن آخر ما تقول)).
فقلت أستذكرهن: وبرسولك الذي أرسلت. قال: ((لا، وبنبيك الذي أرسلت)).
وزاد في رواية: ((وإن أصبحت أصبت خيرًا)).
وفي رواية بعد قوله: ((أسلمت نفسي إليك)) زيادة: ((ووجهت وجهي إليك)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٣١١)، ومسلم (٢٧١٠). والزيادة الأولى والثانية لمسلم.

11232 — Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
“When you go to your bed, perform ablution as you would for prayer. Then lie upon your right side and say: ‘O Allah, I submit myself to You, entrust my affairs to You, and seek support by turning my back toward You, out of fear of You and hope in You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except with You. I believe in Your Book which You revealed and in Your Prophet whom You sent.’ If you die, you will die upon the natural disposition of faith. Make these the final words you say.”
I repeated the words in order to memorize them and said:
“And in Your Messenger whom You sent.”
He corrected me:
“No. Say: ‘And in Your Prophet whom You sent.’”
Another narration adds:
“If you reach the morning, you will attain good.”
Another narration adds after the words “I submit myself to You”:
“And I turn my face toward You.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6311) and Muslim (2710). The two additional wordings were narrated by Muslim.

١١٢٣٧ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر أنه أمر رجلًا إذا أخذ مضجعه أن يقول: ((اللهم خلقت نفسي، وأنت توفاها، لك مماتها ومحياها. إن أحييتها فاحفظها، وإن أمتها فاغفر لها. اللهم إني أسألك العافية)).
فقال له رجل: أسمعت هذا من عمر؟ فقال: من خير من عمر، من رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٧١٢).

11237 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar instructed a man to say when going to bed:
“O Allah, You created my soul, and You will take it. Its death and life belong to You. If You keep it alive, then protect it; and if You cause it to die, then forgive it. O Allah, I ask You for well-being.”
A man asked him:
“Did you hear this from ʿUmar?”
He replied:
“From one better than ʿUmar—from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2712).

١١٢٣٨ — عن سهيل قال: كان أبو صالح يأمرنا إذا أراد أحدنا أن ينام أن يضطجع على شقه الأيمن، ثم يقول: ((اللهم رب السماوات، ورب الأرض، ورب العرش العظيم، ربنا ورب كل شيء، فالق الحب والنوى، ومنزل التوراة والإنجيل والفرقان، أعوذ بك من شر كل شيء أنت آخذ بناصيته. اللهم أنت الأول فليس قبلك شيء، وأنت الآخر فليس بعدك شيء، وأنت الظاهر فليس فوقك شيء، وأنت الباطن فليس دونك شيء، اقض عنا الدين، وأغننا من الفقر)).
وكان يروي ذلك عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٧١٣/٦١).

english_source:
11238 — Suhayl narrated:
Abū Ṣāliḥ used to instruct us that when one of us wished to sleep, he should lie upon his right side and say:
“O Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Mighty Throne; our Lord and Lord of everything; Splitter of the grain and the date-stone; Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion: I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything whose forelock You hold.
O Allah, You are the First, and there is nothing before You. You are the Last, and there is nothing after You. You are the Most High, and there is nothing above You. You are the Innermost, and there is nothing beyond You. Settle our debts and free us from poverty.”
He narrated this from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2713/61).

11239 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“When one of you goes to his bed, let him dust it with the inner edge of his garment, for he does not know what may have come upon it after he left. Then let him say: ‘In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and through You I raise it. If You take my soul, then have mercy upon it; and if You release it, then protect it in the manner by which You protect the righteous.’”
Another narration states:
“When one of you goes to his bed, let him take the inner edge of his garment and dust the bed with it, mentioning Allah’s name, for he does not know what may have come upon the bed after him. When he wishes to lie down, let him lie upon his right side and say: ‘Glory be to You, O Allah, my Lord. Through You I lay down my side, and through You I raise it. If You take my soul, then forgive it; and if You release it, then protect it in the manner by which You protect Your righteous servants.’”
Another narration states:
“When one of you comes to his bed, let him dust it three times with the edge of his garment and say: ‘In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side…’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6320), Muslim (2714/64) with the second wording, and al-Bukhārī (7393) with the third wording.

١١٢٤٠ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: ((إذا قام أحدكم عن فراشه ثم رجع إليه، فلينفضه بصنفة إزاره ثلاث مرات؛ فإنه لا يدري ما خلفه عليه بعد. فإذا اضطجع فليقل: باسمك ربي وضعت جنبي، وبك أرفعه، فإن أمسكت نفسي فارحمها، وإن أرسلتها فاحفظها بما تحفظ به عبادك الصالحين. فإذا استيقظ فليقل: الحمد للّٰه الذي عافاني في جسدي، ورد علي روحي، وأذن لي بذكره)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٤٠١)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٨٦٦)، وابن السني (٩).

11240 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When one of you rises from his bed and later returns to it, let him dust it three times with the edge of his garment, for he does not know what may have come upon it after he left.
When he lies down, let him say: ‘In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and through You I raise it. If You take my soul, then have mercy upon it; and if You release it, then protect it in the manner by which You protect Your righteous servants.’
When he awakens, let him say: ‘All praise belongs to Allah, who granted well-being to my body, returned my soul to me, and permitted me to remember Him.’”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3401), al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (866), and Ibn al-Sunnī (9).

11242 — Anas narrated:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to his bed, he would say:
“All praise belongs to Allah, who fed us, gave us drink, sufficed us, and granted us shelter. How many people have no one to suffice them and no one to shelter them.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2715).

١١٢٤٥ — عن أبي الأزهر الأنماري أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان إذا أخذ مضجعه من الليل قال: ((بسم اللّٰه، وضعت جنبي. اللهم اغفر لي ذنبي، واخسأ شيطاني، وفك رهاني، وثقل ميزاني، واجعلني في الندي الأعلى)).
وفي رواية: ((في الملأ الأعلى)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٥٤)، وابن السني في عمل اليوم والليلة (٧١٨)، وصححه الحاكم (١/٥٤٠، ٥٤٩).
وقوله: «واخسأ شيطاني»، بوصل الهمزة وفتح السين، من خسأت الكلب، أي: طردته، والمعنى: اجعله مطرودًا عني.
وقوله: «الندي الأعلى»، أي: الملأ الأعلى من الملائكة؛ لأن الندي معناه اجتماع القوم في المجلس.

11245 — Abū al-Azhar al-Anmārī narrated:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to bed at night, he would say:
“In the name of Allah, I lay down my side. O Allah, forgive my sin, drive my devil away, release me from my burden, make my scale heavy, and place me among the highest assembly.”
Another narration states:
“Among the highest company.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5054) and Ibn al-Sunnī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (718), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (1/540, 549).
The expression “drive my devil away” comes from the phrase used for expelling a dog. Its meaning is:
“Make Satan rejected and driven away from me.”
The expression “the highest assembly” refers to the highest company of angels, because al-nadī means a gathering of people in an assembly.

١١٢٤٦ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو بكر: يا رسول اللّٰه، مرني بشيء أقوله إذا أصبحت وإذا أمسيت؟ قال: ((قل: اللهم عالم الغيب والشهادة، فاطر السماوات والأرض، رب كل شيء ومليكه، أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت، أعوذ بك من شر نفسي، ومن شر الشيطان وشركه)). قال: ((قله إذا أصبحت، وإذا أمسيت، وإذا أخذت مضجعك)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٦٧)، والترمذي (٣٣٩٢)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (١٢٠٢، ١٢٠٣)، وأحمد (٧٩٦١)، وصححه ابن حبان (٩٦٢)، والحاكم (١/٥١٣).

english_source:
11246 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
Abū Bakr said:
“O Messenger of Allah, instruct me with something to say in the morning and in the evening.”
He said:
“Say: ‘O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of everything, I testify that there is no deity worthy of worship except You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own soul and from the evil of Satan and his polytheistic enticement.’”
He then said:
“Say it in the morning, in the evening, and when you lie down to sleep.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5067), al-Tirmidhī (3392), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (1202, 1203), Aḥmad (7961), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (962) and al-Ḥākim (1/513).

11247 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say when going to bed:
“All praise belongs to Allah, who has sufficed me and sheltered me, fed me and given me drink; who bestowed His favor upon me and made it abundant, and who gave me generously. All praise belongs to Allah in every circumstance. O Allah, Lord and Sovereign of everything and God of everything, I seek refuge in You from the Fire.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5058), Aḥmad (5983), and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (798), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (5538).

“All praise belongs to Allah, who has sufficed me and sheltered me, fed me and given me drink; who bestowed His favor upon me and made it abundant, and who gave me generously. All praise belongs to Allah in every circumstance. O Allah, Lord and Sovereign of everything and God of everything, I seek refuge in You from the Fire.”

١١٢٤٧ — عن ابن عمر أنه حدثه أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان يقول إذا أخذ مضجعه: ((الحمد للّٰه الذي كفاني وآواني، وأطعمني وسقاني، والذي من علي فأفضل، والذي أعطاني فأجزل. الحمد للّٰه على كل حال. اللهم رب كل شيء ومليكه، وإله كل شيء، أعوذ بك من النار)).

١١٢٤٨ — عن أبي هريرة أن فاطمة أتت النبي ﷺ تسأله خادمًا، وشكت العمل، فقال: ((ما ألفيتيه عندنا)). قال: ((ألا أدلك على ما هو خير لك من خادم؟ تسبحين ثلاثًا وثلاثين، وتحمدين ثلاثًا وثلاثين، وتكبرين أربعًا وثلاثين حين تأخذين مضجعك)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٧٢٨).

١١٢٤٩ — عن علي أن فاطمة شكت ما تلقى في يدها من الرحى، فأتت النبي ﷺ تسأله خادمًا، فلم تجده، فذكرت ذلك لعائشة. فلما جاء أخبرته. قال: فجاءنا وقد أخذنا مضاجعنا، فذهبت أقوم، فقال: ((مكانك)). فجلس بيننا حتى وجدت برد قدميه على صدري، فقال: ((ألا أدلكما على ما هو خير لكما من خادم؟ إذا أويتما إلى فراشكما، أو أخذتما مضاجعكما، فكبرا ثلاثًا وثلاثين، وسبحا ثلاثًا وثلاثين، واحمدا ثلاثًا وثلاثين، فهذا خير لكما من خادم)).
وزاد في رواية: قال علي: ما تركته منذ سمعته من النبي ﷺ. قيل له: ولا ليلة صفين؟ قال: ولا ليلة صفين.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٣١٨)، ومسلم (٢٧٢٧).

english_source:
11249 — ʿAlī narrated:
Fāṭimah complained of the hardship her hands suffered from using the hand mill. She went to the Prophet ﷺ to ask him for a servant, but she did not find him, so she mentioned the matter to ʿĀʾishah.
When he returned, ʿĀʾishah informed him.
ʿAlī said:
He came to us after we had gone to bed. I began to rise, but he said:
“Remain where you are.”
He sat between us until I felt the coolness of his feet upon my chest.
He then said:
“Shall I direct both of you to something better for you than a servant? When you go to your bed, or lie down to sleep, proclaim Allah’s greatness thirty-three times, glorify Allah thirty-three times, and praise Allah thirty-three times. This is better for both of you than a servant.”
Another narration adds that ʿAlī said:
“I have never abandoned these words since I heard them from the Prophet ﷺ.”
He was asked:
“Not even on the night of Ṣiffīn?”
He replied:
“Not even on the night of Ṣiffīn.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6318) and Muslim (2727).

١١٢٥٠ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو، عن النبي ﷺ، أنه أمر فاطمة وعليًا إذا أخذا مضاجعهما بالتسبيح والتحميد والتكبير، لا يدري عطاء أيها أربع وثلاثون تمام المائة. قال: فقال علي: فما تركتهن بعد. قال: فقال له ابن الكواء: ولا ليلة صفين؟ قال علي: ولا ليلة صفين.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٦٥٥٤).

11250 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ instructed Fāṭimah and ʿAlī, when they went to bed, to glorify Allah, praise Him, and proclaim His greatness.
ʿAṭāʾ, one of the narrators, was uncertain which of the three was to be recited thirty-four times in order to complete one hundred.
ʿAlī said:
“I never abandoned them afterward.”
Ibn al-Kawwāʾ asked him:
“Not even on the night of Ṣiffīn?”
ʿAlī replied:
“Not even on the night of Ṣiffīn.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (6554).

arabic_source:
١١٢٥١ — عن علي قال: قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، واللّٰه لقد سنوت حتى اشتكيت صدري. وقالت فاطمة: قد طحنت حتى مجلت يداي، وقد جاءك اللّٰه بسبي وسعة، فأخدمنا. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((واللّٰه لا أعطيكما وأدع أهل الصفة تطوى بطونهم، لا أجد ما أنفق عليهم، ولكني أبيعهم وأنفق عليهم أثمانهم)).
فرجعا، فأتاهما النبي ﷺ وقد دخلا في قطيفتهما، إذا غطت رؤوسهما تكشفت أقدامهما، وإذا غطيا أقدامهما تكشفت رؤوسهما. فثارا، فقال: ((مكانكما)).
ثم قال: ((ألا أخبركما بخير مما سألتماني؟)). قالا: بلى. فقال: ((كلمات علمنيهن جبريل، فقال: تسبحان في دبر كل صلاة عشرًا، وتحمدان عشرًا، وتكبران عشرًا، وإذا أويتما إلى فراشكما فسبحا ثلاثًا وثلاثين، واحمدا ثلاثًا وثلاثين، وكبرا أربعًا وثلاثين)).
قال: فواللّٰه ما تركتهن منذ علمنيهن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ. قال: فقال له ابن الكواء: ولا ليلة صفين؟ فقال: قاتلكم اللّٰه يا أهل العراق، نعم، ولا ليلة صفين.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٥٩٦، ٨٣٨)، وابن سعد (٨/٢٥)، والبزار (٧٥٧).

11251 — ʿAlī narrated:
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have drawn water from the well until my chest has begun to ache.”
Fāṭimah said:
“I have ground grain until my hands have developed calluses. Allah has now brought you captives and abundance, so provide us with a servant.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“By Allah, I will not give the two of you servants while leaving the people of al-Ṣuffah with their stomachs folded from hunger, when I have nothing to spend upon them. Rather, I will sell the captives and spend their price upon them.”
They returned home.
The Prophet ﷺ later came to them after they had entered beneath their small blanket. When they covered their heads, their feet became exposed, and when they covered their feet, their heads became exposed.
They began to rise, but he said:
“Remain where you are.”
He then said:
“Shall I inform you of something better than what you asked me for?”
They replied:
“Yes.”
He said:
“These are words Gabriel taught me: after every prayer, glorify Allah ten times, praise Him ten times, and proclaim His greatness ten times. When you go to your bed, glorify Allah thirty-three times, praise Him thirty-three times, and proclaim His greatness thirty-four times.”
ʿAlī said:
“By Allah, I have never abandoned them since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught them to me.”
Ibn al-Kawwāʾ asked him:
“Not even on the night of Ṣiffīn?”
ʿAlī replied:
“May Allah deal with you, people of Iraq! Yes, not even on the night of Ṣiffīn.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (596, 838), Ibn Saʿd (8/25), and al-Bazzār (757).

١١٢٥٢ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((خصلتان أو خلتان لا يحافظ عليهما عبد مسلم إلا دخل الجنة، هما يسير، ومن يعمل بهما قليل: يسبح في دبر كل صلاة عشرًا، ويحمد عشرًا، ويكبر عشرًا، فذلك خمسون ومائة باللسان، وألف وخمسمائة في الميزان. ويكبر أربعًا وثلاثين إذا أخذ مضجعه، ويحمد ثلاثًا وثلاثين، ويسبح ثلاثًا وثلاثين، فذلك مائة باللسان، وألف في الميزان)).
ولقد رأيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يعقدها بيده. قالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، كيف هما يسير، ومن يعمل بهما قليل؟ قال: ((يأتي أحدكم - يعني الشيطان - في منامه فينومه قبل أن يقولها، ويأتيه في صلاته فيذكره حاجة قبل أن يقولها)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٦٥)، والترمذي (٣٤١٠)، والنسائي (١٣٤٨)، وابن ماجه (٩٢٦)، واللفظ لأبي داود.
وقوله: «فتلك خمسون ومائة»، يعني: في خمس مرات في كل يوم وليلة.

11252 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“There are two practices—or two qualities—which no Muslim servant consistently observes except that he will enter Paradise. They are easy, yet those who practice them are few.
After every prayer, he glorifies Allah ten times, praises Allah ten times, and proclaims Allah’s greatness ten times. That amounts to one hundred and fifty upon the tongue and one thousand five hundred in the Scale.
When he goes to bed, he proclaims Allah’s greatness thirty-four times, praises Allah thirty-three times, and glorifies Allah thirty-three times. That amounts to one hundred upon the tongue and one thousand in the Scale.”
The narrator said:
“I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ counting them upon his hand.”
They asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how are they easy while those who practice them are few?”
He replied:
“Satan comes to one of you when he is about to sleep and causes him to fall asleep before he says them. He also comes to him during his prayer and reminds him of some need before he says them.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5065), al-Tirmidhī (3410), al-Nasāʾī (1348), and Ibn Mājah (926). The wording cited here is that of Abū Dāwūd.
The words “that amounts to one hundred and fifty” refer to the five obligatory prayers performed during every day and night.

١١٢٥٣ — عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إذا أوى إلى فراشه نفث في كفيه بـ﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ وبالمعوذتين جميعًا، ثم يمسح بهما وجهه، وما بلغت يداه من جسده.
قالت عائشة: فلما اشتكى كان يأمرني أن أفعل ذلك به.

١١٢٥٤ — عن عائشة أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا أوى إلى فراشه كل ليلة جمع كفيه، ثم نفث فيهما، فقرأ فيهما: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ [سورة الإخلاص: ١]، و﴿قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ﴾ [سورة الفلق: ١]، و﴿قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ﴾ [سورة الناس: ١]، ثم يمسح بهما ما استطاع من جسده، يبدأ بهما على رأسه ووجهه وما أقبل من جسده، يفعل ذلك ثلاث مرات.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٠١٧).
في هذا الحديث أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان يفعل ذلك ثلاث مرات، وفي الرواية السابقة لم يذكر عدد معين، فمن فعل ذلك ثلاثًا فقد أحسن، ومن فعل دون ذلك فلا حرج عليه.

11254 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
Every night, when the Prophet ﷺ went to bed, he would bring his palms together, lightly blow into them, and recite:
“Say: He is Allah, the One,”
 [Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ 112:1]
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak,”
 [Sūrat al-Falaq 113:1]
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.”
 [Sūrat al-Nās 114:1]
He would then wipe with them whatever parts of his body he could reach, beginning with his head, face, and the front of his body. He would do this three times.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5017).
This hadith states that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did this three times. The preceding narration does not specify a particular number. Therefore, whoever does it three times has done well, and whoever does it fewer times bears no blame.

١١٢٥٥ — عن أبي هريرة في قصة حفظ زكاة رمضان، قال: قال لي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((ما فعل أسيرك البارحة؟)). قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه، زعم أنه يعلمني كلمات ينفعني اللّٰه بها، فخليت سبيله. قال: ((ما هي؟)). قلت: قال لي: إذا أويت إلى فراشك، فاقرأ آية الكرسي من أولها حتى تختم الآية: ﴿اللّٰهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ﴾. وقال لي: لن يزال عليك من اللّٰه حافظ، ولا يقربك شيطان حتى تصبح. وكانوا أحرص شيء على الخير. فقال النبي ﷺ: ((أما إنه قد صدقك وهو كذوب. تعلم من تخاطب منذ ثلاث ليال يا أبا هريرة؟)). قال: لا. قال: ((ذاك شيطان)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٣١١).

11255 — Abū Hurayrah narrated, concerning the incident in which he guarded the charity of Ramaḍān:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked me:
“What happened to your captive last night?”
I replied:
“O Messenger of Allah, he claimed that he would teach me words through which Allah would benefit me, so I released him.”
He asked:
“What were they?”
I replied:
“He told me, ‘When you go to bed, recite Āyat al-Kursī from its beginning until you complete the verse:
“Allah—there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all.”
He also told me, ‘A protector from Allah will remain over you, and no devil will approach you until morning.’”
The Companions were the most eager of people for goodness.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“He has spoken the truth to you, although he is a habitual liar. Do you know whom you have been speaking to for the past three nights, O Abū Hurayrah?”
He replied:
“No.”
He said:
“That was a devil.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2311).

“Whoever recites the final two verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah during the night, they will suffice him.”

١١٢٥٧ — عن فروة بن نوفل الأشجعي، عن أبيه، قال: دفع إلي النبي ﷺ ابنة أم سلمة، وقال: ((إنما أنت ظئري)). قال: فمكث ما شاء اللّٰه، ثم أتيته، فقال: ((ما فعلت الجارية، أو الجويرية؟)). قال: قلت: عند أمها. قال: ((فمجيء ما جئت؟)). قال: قلت: تعلمني ما أقول عند منامي. فقال: ((اقرأ عند منامك: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ﴾)). قال: ((ثم نم على خاتمتها؛ فإنها براءة من الشرك)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣٨٠٧)، والترمذي (٣٤٠٣)، وصححه الحاكم (١/٥٦٥).

11257 — Farwah ibn Nawfal al-Ashjaʿī narrated from his father:
The Prophet ﷺ entrusted the daughter of Umm Salamah to me and said:
“You are her foster caretaker.”
He remained away for as long as Allah willed, and then I came to him.
He asked:
“What happened to the girl—or the young girl?”
I replied:
“She is with her mother.”
He asked:
“Then why have you come?”
I said:
“Teach me what I should say when I go to sleep.”
He said:
“When you go to sleep, recite: ‘Say: O disbelievers.’ Then sleep after completing it, for it is a declaration of freedom from polytheism.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (23807), al-Tirmidhī (3403), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (1/565).

١١٢٥٩ — عن جابر قال: كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ لا ينام حتى يقرأ ﴿الم ۝ تَنْزِيلُ﴾ السجدة، و﴿تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ [سورة الملك: ١].
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٨٩٢)، وأحمد (١٤٦٩٥)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (١٢٠٧، ١٢٠٩).
وقوله: «كان لا ينام حتى يقرأ»، يحتمل أن يكون عند إرادة النوم قبل الأذكار الأخرى المعروفة، ويحتمل أن يكون الوقت موسعًا لقراءة هاتين السورتين قبل أن ينام.

english_source:
11259 — Jābir narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not sleep until he had recited Sūrat al-Sajdah, beginning:
“Alif-Lām-Mīm. The revelation…”
and Sūrat al-Mulk, beginning:
“Blessed is the One in whose hand is all dominion, and He has power over all things.”
 [Sūrat al-Mulk 67:1]
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2892), Aḥmad (14695), and al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (1207, 1209).
The words “he would not sleep until he had recited them” may mean that he recited them when preparing to sleep, before the other established remembrances. It may also mean that there was flexibility in reciting these two sūrahs at any time before sleeping.

١١٢٦٠ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((من قال حين يأوي إلى فراشه: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، وهو على كل شيء قدير، لا حول ولا قوة إلا باللّٰه، سبحان اللّٰه، والحمد للّٰه، ولا إله إلا اللّٰه، واللّٰه أكبر، غفر اللّٰه ذنوبه أو خطاياه، وإن كانت مثل زبد البحر)).
صحيح: رواه ابن حبان (٥٥٢٨)، وابن السني في عمل اليوم والليلة (٧٢٤).

11260 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever says when going to bed, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things. There is no power and no strength except through Allah. Glory be to Allah, all praise belongs to Allah, there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest,’ Allah will forgive his sins—or his errors—even if they are as abundant as the foam of the sea.”
Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān (5528) and Ibn al-Sunnī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (724).

11261 — Jābir narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When a man goes to his bed, an angel and a devil come to him. The angel says, ‘End your day with good,’ while the devil says, ‘End it with evil.’
If he remembers Allah and then sleeps, the angels spend the night guarding him. When he awakens, the angel says, ‘Begin with good,’ while the devil says, ‘Begin with evil.’
If he says, ‘All praise belongs to Allah, who returned my soul to me and did not cause it to die during its sleep. All praise belongs to Allah, who holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease, and if they were to cease, none could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is Most Forbearing, Most Forgiving. All praise belongs to Allah, who holds the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission,’ then if he falls from his bed and dies, he will enter Paradise.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā (1791), through him by Ibn Ḥibbān (5533), and by al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (378).

١١٢٦٢ — عن جابر، عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أنه قال: ((إذا رأى أحدكم الرؤيا يكرهها، فليبصق عن يساره ثلاثًا، وليستعذ باللّٰه من الشيطان ثلاثًا، وليتحول عن جنبه الذي كان عليه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٦٢).

11262 — Jābir narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“When one of you sees a dream he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times, seek refuge in Allah from Satan three times, and turn over from the side upon which he had been lying.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2262).

١١٢٦٣ — عن عبادة بن الصامت، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((من تعار من الليل فقال: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد، وهو على كل شيء قدير، الحمد للّٰه، وسبحان اللّٰه، ولا إله إلا اللّٰه، واللّٰه أكبر، ولا حول ولا قوة إلا باللّٰه، ثم قال: اللهم اغفر لي، أو دعا، استجيب له. فإن توضأ وصلى، قبلت صلاته)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١١٥٤).
قوله: «تعار»، التعار: التقلب على الفراش ليلًا مع كلام، وقال الأكثر: التعار اليقظة. الفتح (٣/٤٠).
وقوله: ((فإن توضأ وصلى قبلت صلاته)) توضحه رواية الترمذي (٣٤١٤): ((فإن عزم وتوضأ ثم صلى، قبلت صلاته)).

11263 — ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Whoever awakens during the night and says, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He has power over all things. All praise belongs to Allah, glory be to Allah, there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and there is no power and no strength except through Allah,’ and then says, ‘O Allah, forgive me,’ or makes any supplication, it will be answered. If he performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1154).
The expression taʿārra means turning about in bed during the night while speaking. Most scholars explained it as awakening from sleep. Fatḥ al-Bārī (3/40).
The words “If he performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted” are clarified by the narration of al-Tirmidhī (3414):
“If he resolves to do so, performs ablution, and then prays, his prayer will be accepted.”

11264 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ awoke during the night, he would say:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except You. Glory be to You, O Allah. I seek Your forgiveness for my sin and ask You for Your mercy. O Allah, increase me in knowledge, do not cause my heart to deviate after You have guided me, and grant me mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower.”

١١٢٦٥ — عن ابن عباس أنه بات ليلة عند ميمونة زوج النبي ﷺ، وهي خالته، قال: فاضطجعت في عرض الوسادة، واضطجع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وأهله في طولها. فنام رسول اللّٰه ﷺ حتى إذا انتصف الليل، أو قبله بقليل، أو بعده بقليل، استيقظ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فجلس يمسح النوم عن وجهه بيده، ثم قرأ العشر الآيات الخواتم من سورة آل عمران، وهي قوله تعالى: ﴿إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ لَآيَاتٍ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ إلى قوله تعالى: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اصْبِرُوا وَصَابِرُوا وَرَابِطُوا وَاتَّقُوا اللّٰهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ [سورة آل عمران: ١٩٠-٢٠٠].
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (١١)، والبخاري (٤٥٧٢)، ومسلم (٧٦٣/١٨٢).

11265 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
I spent one night at the home of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, who was my maternal aunt.
I lay across the width of the pillow, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his wife lay along its length.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept until approximately midnight—either a little before or a little after it. He then awoke, sat up, and wiped the effects of sleep from his face with his hand.
He then recited the final ten verses of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, beginning with:
“Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for people of understanding,”
and continuing until:
“O you who believe, be patient, outlast others in patience, remain stationed, and be mindful of Allah so that you may succeed.”
 [Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:190–200]
Agreed upon: Narrated by Mālik (11), al-Bukhārī (4572), and Muslim (763/182).

١١٢٦٦ — عن عائشة أنها قالت: كان النبي ﷺ إذا عصفت الريح قال: ((اللهم إني أسألك خيرها، وخير ما فيها، وخير ما أرسلت به، وأعوذ بك من شرها، وشر ما فيها، وشر ما أرسلت به)).
قالت: وإذا تخيلت السماء تغير لونه، وخرج ودخل، وأقبل وأدبر، فإذا مطرت سري عنه، فعرفت ذلك في وجهه. قالت عائشة: فسألته، فقال: ((لعله يا عائشة كما قال قوم عاد: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضًا مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قَالُوا هَذَا عَارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنَا﴾ [سورة الأحقاف: ٢٤])).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٢٠٦)، ومسلم (٨٩٩/١٥).

11266 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
When the wind blew violently, the Prophet ﷺ would say:
“O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good contained within it, and the good with which it was sent. I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil contained within it, and the evil with which it was sent.”
She said:
When clouds gathered in the sky, his complexion would change. He would go out and come back in, moving forward and backward. When rain fell, his concern would be relieved, and I could recognize that upon his face.
ʿĀʾishah said:
I asked him about this, and he replied:
“Perhaps, O ʿĀʾishah, it may be like what the people of ʿĀd said: ‘When they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, “This is a cloud bringing us rain.”’”
 [Sūrat al-Aḥqāf 46:24]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3206) and Muslim (899/15).

11267 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The wind is from the mercy of Allah. It may bring mercy or punishment. Therefore, do not curse it. Rather, ask Allah for its good and seek refuge in Allah from its evil.”

١١٢٦٨ — عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((لا تسبوا الريح، فإذا رأيتم ما تكرهون فقولوا: اللهم إنا نسألك من خير هذه الريح، وخير ما فيها، وخير ما أمرت به، ونعوذ بك من شر هذه الريح، وشر ما فيها، وشر ما أمرت به)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٢٥٢)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٩٣٤)، وعبد اللّٰه بن أحمد في زوائد المسند (٢١١٣٩)، والطحاوي في شرح مشكل الآثار (٩١٨).

11268 — Ubayy ibn Kaʿb narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Do not curse the wind. When you see from it something you dislike, say: ‘O Allah, we ask You for the good of this wind, the good contained within it, and the good it has been commanded to bring. We seek refuge in You from the evil of this wind, the evil contained within it, and the evil it has been commanded to bring.’”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2252), al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (934), ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad in Zawāʾid al-Musnad (21139), and al-Ṭaḥāwī in Sharḥ Mushkil al-Āthār (918).

١١٢٦٩ — عن أنس قال: كان النبي ﷺ إذا هاجت ريح شديدة قال: ((اللهم إني أسألك من خير ما أرسلت به، وأعوذ بك من شر ما أرسلت به)).

11269 — Anas narrated:
When a strong wind arose, the Prophet ﷺ would say:
“O Allah, I ask You for the good with which it was sent, and I seek refuge in You from the evil with which it was sent.”
Another narration adds at the beginning:
“Whenever he saw the wind, he became apprehensive.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (717), Abū Yaʿlā (2905), and al-Ṭaḥāwī in Sharḥ Mushkil al-Āthār (926).

arabic_source:
١١٢٧١ — عن عائشة أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا رأى سحابًا مقبلًا من أفق من الآفاق، ترك ما هو فيه، وإن كان في صلاته، حتى يستقبله، فيقول: ((اللهم إنا نعوذ بك من شر ما أرسل به)). فإن أمطر قال: ((اللهم سيبًا نافعًا)) مرتين أو ثلاثًا. وإن كشفه اللّٰه عز وجل ولم يمطر، حمد اللّٰه على ذلك.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٩٩)، وابن ماجه (٣٨٨٩)، وأحمد (٢٥٥٧٠)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٦٨٦)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٩١٤، ٩١٥)، وصححه ابن حبان (٩٩٤).
وقوله: «سيبًا»، أي: مطرًا سائبًا، وهو الجاري. و«صيبًا» معناه: متدفقًا، وأصله الواو؛ لأنه من صاب يصوب إذا نزل.

english_source:
11271 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
When the Prophet ﷺ saw clouds approaching from any direction, he would leave whatever he was occupied with—even if he was praying—until he faced them and said:
“O Allah, we seek refuge in You from the evil with which they have been sent.”
If rain fell, he would say two or three times:
“O Allah, make it a beneficial, flowing rain.”
If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, dispersed the clouds without rain, he would praise Allah for that.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5099), Ibn Mājah (3889), Aḥmad (25570), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (686), and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (914, 915), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (994).
The word sayyiban means flowing rain. The word ṣayyiban means rain pouring down abundantly. Its linguistic root contains the letter wāw, deriving from the verb meaning “to descend.”

١١٢٧١ — عن عائشة أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا رأى سحابًا مقبلًا من أفق من الآفاق، ترك ما هو فيه، وإن كان في صلاته، حتى يستقبله، فيقول: ((اللهم إنا نعوذ بك من شر ما أرسل به)). فإن أمطر قال: ((اللهم سيبًا نافعًا)) مرتين أو ثلاثًا. وإن كشفه اللّٰه عز وجل ولم يمطر، حمد اللّٰه على ذلك.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٩٩)، وابن ماجه (٣٨٨٩)، وأحمد (٢٥٥٧٠)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٦٨٦)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٩١٤، ٩١٥)، وصححه ابن حبان (٩٩٤).
وقوله: «سيبًا»، أي: مطرًا سائبًا، وهو الجاري. و«صيبًا» معناه: متدفقًا، وأصله الواو؛ لأنه من صاب يصوب إذا نزل.
11271 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
When the Prophet ﷺ saw clouds approaching from any direction, he would leave whatever he was occupied with—even if he was praying—until he faced them and said:
“O Allah, we seek refuge in You from the evil with which they have been sent.”
If rain fell, he would say two or three times:
“O Allah, make it a beneficial, flowing rain.”
If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, dispersed the clouds without rain, he would praise Allah for that.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5099), Ibn Mājah (3889), Aḥmad (25570), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (686), and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (914, 915), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (994).

١١٢٧٤ — عن سليمان بن صرد قال: استب رجلان عند النبي ﷺ، فجعل أحدهما يغضب ويحمر وجهه، فنظر إليه النبي ﷺ فقال: ((إني لأعلم كلمة لو قالها لذهب ذا عنه: أعوذ باللّٰه من الشيطان الرجيم)).
فقام إلى الرجل رجل ممن سمع النبي ﷺ، فقال: أتدري ما قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ آنفًا؟ قال: ((إني لأعلم كلمة لو قالها لذهب ذا عنه: أعوذ باللّٰه من الشيطان الرجيم)). فقال له الرجل: أمجنونًا تراني؟
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١١٥)، ومسلم (٢٦١٠/١١٠).

11274 — Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad narrated:
Two men insulted one another in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ. One of them became angry, and his face turned red.
The Prophet ﷺ looked at him and said:
“I know a phrase which, if he were to say it, would remove what he is experiencing: ‘I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed.’”
A man who had heard the Prophet ﷺ went to him and said:
“Do you know what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ just said? He said, ‘I know a phrase which, if he were to say it, would remove what he is experiencing: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed.’”
The angry man replied:
“Do you think I am insane?”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6115) and Muslim (2610/110).

11276 — Abū Bakrah narrated:
A man praised another man in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ.
He said three times:
“Woe to you! You have cut your brother’s neck.”
He then said:
“If one of you must praise someone, let him say: ‘I consider so-and-so to be such-and-such, and Allah is his Reckoner. I do not declare anyone pure before Allah,’ if he knows that to be true of him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6162) and Muslim (3000).

١١٢٧٦ — عن أبي بكرة قال: أثنى رجل على رجل عند النبي ﷺ، فقال: ((ويلك، قطعت عنق أخيك)) ثلاثًا. ((من كان منكم مادحًا لا محالة، فليقل: أحسب فلانًا، واللّٰه حسيبه، ولا أزكي على اللّٰه أحدًا، إن كان يعلم)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٦٢)، ومسلم (٣٠٠٠).
11276 — Abū Bakrah narrated:
A man praised another man in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ.
He said three times:
“Woe to you! You have cut your brother’s neck.”
He then said:
“If one of you must praise someone, let him say: ‘I consider so-and-so to be such-and-such, and Allah is his Reckoner. I do not declare anyone pure before Allah,’ if he knows that to be true of him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6162) and Muslim (3000).

١١٢٧٨ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: حلفت باللات والعزى، فقال أصحابي: قد قلت هجرًا. فأتيت النبي ﷺ فقلت: إن العهد كان قريبًا، وإني حلفت باللات والعزى. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((قل: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده، ثلاثًا، ثم انفث عن يسارك ثلاثًا، وتعوذ، ولا تعد)).
صحيح: رواه النسائي (٣٧٧٦)، وابن ماجه (٢٠٩٧)، وأحمد (١٥٨٩)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٣٦٤).
ومعنى الحديث أن من حلف باللات والعزى فكأنه جعل للّٰه ندًّا، فليستدرك بقوله: لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده، ثلاثًا، ويتعوذ باللّٰه من الشيطان الرجيم؛ فإنه بهذا سيعود إلى التوحيد، ويذهب عنه وسواس الشيطان.

11278 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ narrated:
I swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā. My companions said:
“You have spoken an offensive word.”
I went to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“The time since the pre-Islamic period is still recent, and I swore by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Say three times, ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone.’ Then spit lightly to your left three times, seek refuge in Allah, and do not do it again.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī (3776), Ibn Mājah (2097), and Aḥmad (1589), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (4364).
The meaning of the hadith is that whoever swears by al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā has spoken as though assigning a rival to Allah. He should therefore correct this by saying three times:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone.”
He should also seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed. In this way, he returns to pure monotheism and Satan’s whispering is removed from him.

١١٢٧٩ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((من ردته الطيرة عن حاجة فقد أشرك)). قالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه، ما كفارة ذلك؟ قال: ((أن يقول أحدهم: اللهم لا خير إلا خيرك، ولا طير إلا طيرك، ولا إله غيرك)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٧٠٤٥).

11279 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever is prevented by superstition from fulfilling a need has committed an act of polytheism.”
They asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what is its expiation?”
He replied:
“Let him say: ‘O Allah, there is no good except Your good, no omen except what You decree, and there is no deity other than You.’”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (7045).

11280 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
During times of distress, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6346) and Muslim (2730).

11281 — ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me that when distress befalls me, I should say:
“There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, and blessed is Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (721, 726), al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (630), and Ibn al-Sunnī (342), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (865) and al-Ḥākim (1/508).

11282 — Abū Bakrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“The supplications of a distressed person are: ‘O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for. Do not leave me in charge of myself even for the blink of an eye. Set right all of my affairs. There is no deity worthy of worship except You.’”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5090), Aḥmad (20430), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (701), and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (651), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (970).

11283 — Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
“Shall I teach you words to say during distress—or when afflicted by distress? ‘Allah, Allah is my Lord. I do not associate anything with Him.’”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1525), Ibn Mājah (3882), al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (649), and Aḥmad (27082).

١١٢٨٥ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((دعوة ذي النون إذ دعا وهو في بطن الحوت: ﴿لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾، فإنه لم يدع بها رجل مسلم في شيء قط إلا استجاب اللّٰه له)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٥٠٥)، وأحمد (١٤٦٣)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٦٥٦)، والحاكم (٢/٣٨٢-٣٨٣).
وعند أحمد في أوله قصة: قال سعد: مررت بعثمان بن عفان في المسجد، فسلمت عليه، فملأ عينيه مني ثم لم يرد علي السلام. فأتيت أمير المؤمنين عمر بن الخطاب، فقلت: يا أمير المؤمنين، هل حدث في الإسلام شيء؟ مرتين. قال: لا، وما ذاك؟ قال: قلت: لا، إلا أني مررت بعثمان آنفًا في المسجد، فسلمت عليه، فملأ عينيه مني ثم لم يرد علي السلام.
قال: فأرسل عمر إلى عثمان فدعاه، فقال: ما منعك ألا تكون رددت على أخيك السلام؟ قال عثمان: ما فعلت. قال سعد: قلت: بلى. قال: حتى حلف وحلفت.
قال: ثم إن عثمان ذكر، فقال: بلى، وأستغفر اللّٰه وأتوب إليه. إنك مررت بي آنفًا وأنا أحدث نفسي بكلمة سمعتها من رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، لا واللّٰه، ما ذكرتها قط إلا تغشى بصري وقلبي غشاوة.
قال سعد: فأنا أنبئك بها. إن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ذكر لنا أول دعوة، ثم جاء أعرابي فشغله حتى قام رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فاتبعته. فلما أشفقت أن يسبقني إلى منزله ضربت بقدمي الأرض، فالتفت إلي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال: ((من هذا، أبو إسحاق؟)). قال: قلت: نعم يا رسول اللّٰه. قال: ((فمه؟)). قال: قلت: لا واللّٰه، إلا أنك ذكرت لنا أول دعوة، ثم جاء هذا الأعرابي فشغلك.
قال: ((نعم، دعوة ذي النون إذ هو في بطن الحوت: ﴿لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ٨٧]، فإنه لم يدع بها مسلم ربه في شيء قط إلا استجاب له)).

11285 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The supplication of Dhū al-Nūn when he called upon Allah from within the belly of the fish was: ‘There is no deity worthy of worship except You. Glory be to You. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.’ No Muslim man supplicates with these words concerning anything except that Allah answers him.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3505), Aḥmad (1463), al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (656), and al-Ḥākim (2/382–383).
In Aḥmad’s narration, the following incident precedes the hadith:
Saʿd said:
I passed by ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān in the mosque and greeted him. He looked directly at me but did not return my greeting.

١١٢٨٥ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((دعوة ذي النون إذ دعا وهو في بطن الحوت: ﴿لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾، فإنه لم يدع بها رجل مسلم في شيء قط إلا استجاب اللّٰه له)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٥٠٥)، وأحمد (١٤٦٣)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٦٥٦)، والحاكم (٢/٣٨٢-٣٨٣).

قال: فأرسل عمر إلى عثمان فدعاه، فقال: ما منعك ألا تكون رددت على أخيك السلام؟ قال عثمان: ما فعلت. قال سعد: قلت: بلى. قال: حتى حلف وحلفت.
قال: ثم إن عثمان ذكر، فقال: بلى، وأستغفر اللّٰه وأتوب إليه. إنك مررت بي آنفًا وأنا أحدث نفسي بكلمة سمعتها من رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، لا واللّٰه، ما ذكرتها قط إلا تغشى بصري وقلبي غشاوة.

١١٢٨٦ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ لأبي طلحة: ((التمس لنا غلامًا من غلمانكم يخدمني)). فخرج بي أبو طلحة يردفني وراءه، فكنت أخدم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كلما نزل، فكنت أسمعه يكثر أن يقول: ((اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الهم والحزن، والعجز والكسل، والبخل والجبن، وضلع الدين، وغلبة الرجال)). الحديث.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٣٦٣)، ومسلم (١٣٦٥).

11286 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abū Ṭalḥah:
“Find a boy from among your young servants to serve me.”
Abū Ṭalḥah took me with him, seating me behind him upon his mount. I thereafter served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whenever he stopped.
I frequently heard him say:
“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, incapacity and laziness, miserliness and cowardice, the burden of debt, and being overpowered by men.”
This forms part of the hadith.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6363) and Muslim (1365).

11287 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“No servant is ever afflicted by worry, distress, or grief and then says: ‘O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, and the son of Your female servant. My forelock is in Your hand. Your judgment over me is certain, and Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every name belonging to You, with which You named Yourself, revealed in Your Book, taught to any of Your creation, or kept exclusively with Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen, to make the Qur’an the springtime of my heart, the light of my chest, the removal of my grief, and the departure of my worry and distress,’ except that Allah removes his worry and distress and replaces them with joy.”

١١٢٨٨ — عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((إن اللّٰه يحب العطاس، ويكره التثاؤب، فإذا عطس فحمد اللّٰه، فحق على كل مسلم سمعه أن يشمته. وأما التثاؤب فإنما هو من الشيطان، فليرده ما استطاع، فإذا قال: ها، ضحك منه الشيطان)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٢٢٣)، ومسلم (٢٩٩٤).

11288 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Allah loves sneezing and dislikes yawning. When a person sneezes and praises Allah, every Muslim who hears him has the duty to supplicate for him. As for yawning, it is from Satan, so let him suppress it as much as he can. When he makes the sound ‘hā,’ Satan laughs at him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6223) and Muslim (2994).

11289 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“When one of you sneezes, let him say, ‘All praise belongs to Allah.’ Let his brother or companion say to him, ‘May Allah have mercy upon you.’ When he says, ‘May Allah have mercy upon you,’ let the one who sneezed reply, ‘May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.’”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6224).

صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٩٩٣).

11290 — Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ narrated:
A man sneezed in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to him:
“May Allah have mercy upon you.”
The man then sneezed again, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The man has a cold.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2993).

11291 — Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī narrated from Abū Hurayrah—and he believed that Abū Hurayrah attributed it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—that he said:
“A Muslim who sneezes should be supplicated for up to three times. If he continues sneezing after that, it is a cold.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5035) and Ibn al-Sunnī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (251).

١١٢٩٢ — عن نافع قال: رأيت ابن عمر وقد عطس رجل إلى جنبه، فقال: الحمد للّٰه، وسلام على رسول اللّٰه. فقال ابن عمر: وأنا أقول: السلام على رسول اللّٰه، ولكن ليس هكذا أمرنا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ. أمرنا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن نقول إذا عطسنا: ((الحمد للّٰه على كل حال)).
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الأوسط (٥٦٩٤).

11292 — Nāfiʿ narrated:
I saw Ibn ʿUmar when a man beside him sneezed and said:
“All praise belongs to Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah.”
Ibn ʿUmar said:
“I too say, ‘Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah,’ but this is not how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed us to say when we sneeze:
‘All praise belongs to Allah in every circumstance.’”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ (5694).

١١٢٩٢ — عن نافع قال: رأيت ابن عمر وقد عطس رجل إلى جنبه، فقال: الحمد للّٰه، وسلام على رسول اللّٰه. فقال ابن عمر: وأنا أقول: السلام على رسول اللّٰه، ولكن ليس هكذا أمرنا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ. أمرنا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن نقول إذا عطسنا: ((الحمد للّٰه على كل حال)).
حسن: رواه الطبراني في الأوسط (٥٦٩٤).
11292 — Nāfiʿ narrated:
I saw Ibn ʿUmar when a man beside him sneezed and said:
“All praise belongs to Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah.”
Ibn ʿUmar said:
“I too say, ‘Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah,’ but this is not how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ instructed us to say when we sneeze:
‘All praise belongs to Allah in every circumstance.’”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ (5694).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٢٢٥)، ومسلم (٢٩٩١).

11293 — Anas narrated:
Two men sneezed in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ. He supplicated for one of them but did not supplicate for the other.
The second man said:
“O Messenger of Allah, you supplicated for this man but did not supplicate for me.”
He replied:
“This man praised Allah, while you did not praise Allah.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6225) and Muslim (2991).

١١٢٩٤ — عن أبي بردة قال: دخلت على أبي موسى، وهو في بيت بنت الفضل بن عباس، فعطست فلم يشمتني، وعطست فشمتها. فرجعت إلى أمي فأخبرتها. فلما جاءها قالت: عطس عندك ابني فلم تشمته، وعطست فشمتها؟ فقال: إن ابنك عطس فلم يحمد اللّٰه، فلم أشمته، وعطست فحمدت اللّٰه فشمتها. سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: ((إذا عطس أحدكم فحمد اللّٰه فشمتوه، فإن لم يحمد اللّٰه فلا تشمتوه)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٩٩٢).

11294 — Abū Burdah narrated:
I entered upon Abū Mūsā while he was in the home of the daughter of al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās. I sneezed, but he did not supplicate for me. She sneezed, and he supplicated for her.
I returned to my mother and informed her. When Abū Mūsā later came to her, she said:
“My son sneezed in your presence, but you did not supplicate for him, while she sneezed and you supplicated for her.”
He replied:
“Your son sneezed but did not praise Allah, so I did not supplicate for him. She sneezed and praised Allah, so I supplicated for her. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘When one of you sneezes and praises Allah, supplicate for him. If he does not praise Allah, do not supplicate for him.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2992).

١١٢٩٥ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: كان اليهود يتعاطسون عند النبي ﷺ، يرجون أن يقول لهم: يرحمكم اللّٰه. فيقول: ((يهديكم اللّٰه ويصلح بالكم)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٥٠٣٨)، والترمذي (٢٧٣٩)، وأحمد (١٩٥٨٦)، والبخاري في الأدب المفرد (٩٤٠)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٢٣٢/م)، وصححه الحاكم (٤/٢٦٨).

11295 — Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī narrated:
The Jews would deliberately sneeze in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, hoping that he would say to them:
“May Allah have mercy upon you.”
Instead, he would say:
“May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (5038), al-Tirmidhī (2739), Aḥmad (19586), al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (940), and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (232/M), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (4/268).

١١٢٩٦ — عن أبي وائل قال: أتى عليًّا رجل فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين، إني عجزت عن مكاتبتي فأعني. فقال علي: ألا أعلمك كلمات علمنيهن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، لو كان عليك مثل جبل صير دنانير لأداه اللّٰه عنك؟ قلت: بلى. قال: قل: ((اللهم اكفني بحلالك عن حرامك، وأغنني بفضلك عمن سواك)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٥٦٣)، وعبد اللّٰه بن أحمد في زوائد المسند (١٣١٩)، والحاكم (١/٥٣٨)، وعنه البيهقي في الدعوات الكبير (٣٠٣).
وقوله: «جبل صير»، اسم جبل لطيئ، ويقال: صور، وصير.

11296 — Abū Wāʾil narrated:
A man came to ʿAlī and said:
“O Commander of the Believers, I am unable to fulfill the payment required for my emancipation contract, so help me.”
ʿAlī replied:
“Shall I teach you words that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me? Even if you owed an amount of gold equal to Mount Ṣīr, Allah would repay it on your behalf.”
The man said:
“Yes.”
ʿAlī said:
“Say: ‘O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful instead of what You have forbidden, and enrich me through Your bounty so that I need no one besides You.’”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3563), ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad in Zawāʾid al-Musnad (1319), and al-Ḥākim (1/538), and through him by al-Bayhaqī in al-Daʿawāt al-Kabīr (303).
“Mount Ṣīr” is the name of a mountain belonging to the tribe of Ṭayyiʾ. It is also pronounced Ṣūr or Ṣayr.

The man said:
“Yes.”
ʿAlī said:
“Say: ‘O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful instead of what You have forbidden, and enrich me through Your bounty so that I need no one besides You.’”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3563), ʿAbdullāh ibn Aḥmad in Zawāʾid al-Musnad (1319), and al-Ḥākim (1/538), and through him by al-Bayhaqī in al-Daʿawāt al-Kabīr (303).
“Mount Ṣīr” is the name of a mountain belonging to the tribe of Ṭayyiʾ. It is also pronounced Ṣūr or Ṣayr.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Muʿādh ibn Jabal:
“Shall I teach you a supplication which, if you owed a debt equal to Mount Uḥud, Allah would repay it on your behalf? Say, O Muʿādh:

١١٢٩٨ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ لأبي طلحة: ((التمس لنا غلامًا من غلمانكم يخدمني)). فخرج بي أبو طلحة يردفني وراءه، فكنت أخدم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كلما نزل، فكنت أسمعه يكثر أن يقول: ((اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الهم والحزن، والعجز والكسل، والبخل والجبن، وضلع الدين، وغلبة الرجال)). الحديث.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٣٦٣)، ومسلم (١٣٦٥).

11298 — Anas ibn Mālik narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abū Ṭalḥah:
“Find for us a boy from among your servants who can serve me.”
Abū Ṭalḥah took me with him, seating me behind him on his mount. I thereafter served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whenever he stopped.
I often heard him say:
“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, incapacity and laziness, miserliness and cowardice, the burden of debt, and being overpowered by men.”
This forms part of the hadith.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6363) and Muslim (1365).

١١٢٩٩ — عن أبي مالك الأشجعي، عن أبيه، قال: كان الرجل إذا أسلم علمه النبي ﷺ الصلاة، ثم أمره أن يدعو بهؤلاء الكلمات: ((اللهم اغفر لي، وارحمني، واهدني، وعافني، وارزقني)).
وفي لفظ: أنه سمع النبي ﷺ وأتاه رجل، فقال: يا رسول اللّٰه، كيف أقول حين أسأل ربي؟ قال: ((قل: اللهم اغفر لي، وارحمني، وعافني، وارزقني)). ويجمع أصابعه إلا الإبهام، ((فإن هؤلاء تجمع لك دنياك وآخرتك)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٦٩٧/٣٥) باللفظ الأول، ورواه (٢٦٩٧/٣٦) باللفظ الثاني.

11299 — Abū Mālik al-Ashjaʿī narrated from his father:
When a man accepted Islam, the Prophet ﷺ would teach him the prayer and then instruct him to supplicate with these words:
“O Allah, forgive me, have mercy upon me, guide me, grant me well-being, and provide for me.”
Another wording states that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, what should I say when I ask my Lord?”
He replied:
“Say: ‘O Allah, forgive me, have mercy upon me, grant me well-being, and provide for me.’”
He gathered his fingers together except for the thumb and said:
“These words gather for you the good of this world and the Hereafter.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2697/35) with the first wording and Muslim (2697/36) with the second.

١١٣٠٠ — عن عمران بن حصين أن حصينًا أتى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال: يا محمد، لعبد المطلب كان خيرًا لقومه منك، كان يطعمهم الكبد والسنام، وأنت تنحرهم. فقال له النبي ﷺ ما شاء اللّٰه أن يقول، فقال له: ما تأمرني أن أقول؟ قال: ((قل: اللهم قني شر نفسي، واعزم لي على أرشد أمري)).
قال: فانطلق فأسلم الرجل، ثم جاء فقال: إني أتيتك فقلت لي: قل: ((اللهم قني شر نفسي، واعزم لي على أرشد أمري)). فما أقول الآن؟ قال: ((قل: اللهم اغفر لي ما أسررت، وما أعلنت، وما أخطأت، وما عمدت، وما علمت، وما جهلت)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٩٩٩٢)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (٩٩٤)، وصححه ابن حبان (٨٩٩).

11300 — ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn narrated:
Ḥuṣayn came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Muḥammad, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was better for his people than you. He used to feed them liver and camel hump, whereas you slaughter them.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied to him with what Allah willed him to say.
Ḥuṣayn then asked:
“What do you instruct me to say?”
He replied:
“Say: ‘O Allah, protect me from the evil of my own soul and firmly guide me to the most rightly guided course in my affairs.’”
The man left and accepted Islam. He later returned and said:
“I came to you before, and you told me to say: ‘O Allah, protect me from the evil of my own soul and firmly guide me to the most rightly guided course in my affairs.’ What should I say now?”
He replied:
“Say: ‘O Allah, forgive me for what I concealed and what I made public, what I did mistakenly and what I did deliberately, what I knew and what I did not know.’”

١١٣٠١ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((يأتي الشيطان أحدكم فيقول: من خلق هذا؟ من خلق كذا؟ حتى يقول: من خلق ربك؟ فإذا بلغه فليستعذ باللّٰه ولينته)).
وفي رواية: ((فليقل: آمنت باللّٰه ورسله)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٢٧٦)، ومسلم (١٣٤)، واللفظ للبخاري. والرواية الثانية عند مسلم (١٣٤/٢١٢).

11301 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Satan comes to one of you and says, ‘Who created this? Who created that?’ until he says, ‘Who created your Lord?’ When he reaches that point, let him seek refuge in Allah and stop thinking about it.”
Another narration states:
“Let him say: ‘I believe in Allah and His messengers.’”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3276) and Muslim (134). The cited wording is that of al-Bukhārī. The second wording was narrated by Muslim (134/212).

١١٣٠٢ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ كان يؤتى بأول الثمر، فيقول: ((اللهم بارك لنا في مدينتنا، وفي ثمارنا، وفي مدنا، وفي صاعنا، بركة مع بركة)). ثم يعطيه أصغر من يحضره من الولدان.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٣٧٣/٤٧٤).

english_source:
11302 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The first fruit of the season would be brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would say:
“O Allah, bless us in our city, bless us in our fruits, bless us in our mudd, and bless us in our ṣāʿ—blessing upon blessing.”
He would then give it to the youngest child present.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1373/474).

11303 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever sees a person afflicted and says, ‘All praise belongs to Allah, who granted me well-being from what He afflicted you with and greatly favored me above many of those He created,’ will not be afflicted by that same trial.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ, Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn (4600), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Duʿāʾ (798).

١١٣٠٤ — عن جابر بن عبد اللّٰه أنه سمع النبي ﷺ يقول: ((إذا دخل الرجل بيته فذكر اللّٰه عند دخوله وعند طعامه، قال الشيطان: لا مبيت لكم ولا عشاء. وإذا دخل فلم يذكر اللّٰه عند دخوله، قال الشيطان: أدركتم المبيت. وإذا لم يذكر اللّٰه عند طعامه، قال: أدركتم المبيت والعشاء)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٠١٨/١٠٣).
وقوله: «قال الشيطان»، أي: لرفقائه وأعوانه.

english_source:
11304 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh narrated that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“When a man enters his home and mentions Allah at the time of entering and when eating, Satan says, ‘You have no lodging and no evening meal.’ If he enters without mentioning Allah, Satan says, ‘You have secured lodging.’ If he also fails to mention Allah when eating, Satan says, ‘You have secured both lodging and an evening meal.’”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2018/103).
The words “Satan says” mean that he says this to his companions and helpers.

١١٣٠٥ — عن أم سلمة أن النبي ﷺ كان إذا خرج من بيته قال: ((بسم اللّٰه، توكلت على اللّٰه. اللهم إنا نعوذ بك من أن نزل أو نضل، أو نظلم أو نظلم، أو نجهل أو يجهل علينا)).

When the Prophet ﷺ left his home, he would say:

١١٣٠٦ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((من استعاذ باللّٰه فأعيذوه، ومن سأل باللّٰه فأعطوه، ومن دعاكم فأجيبوه، ومن صنع إليكم معروفًا فكافئوه، فإن لم تجدوا ما تكافئونه، فادعوا له حتى تروا أنكم قد كافأتموه)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (١٦٧٢، ٥١٠٩)، والنسائي (٢٥٦٨)، وأحمد (٥٣٦٥)، وصححه ابن حبان (٣٤٠٨)، والحاكم (٢/٦٣-٦٤).

11306 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever seeks refuge with Allah, grant him refuge. Whoever asks you by Allah, give to him. Whoever invites you, respond to him. Whoever does you a favor, repay him. If you cannot find anything with which to repay him, then supplicate for him until you believe that you have adequately repaid him.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1672, 5109), al-Nasāʾī (2568), Aḥmad (5365), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (3408) and al-Ḥākim (2/63–64).

١١٣٠٧ — عن أسامة بن زيد قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((من صنع إليه معروف فقال لفاعله: جزاك اللّٰه خيرًا، فقد أبلغ في الثناء)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٠٣٥)، والنسائي في عمل اليوم والليلة (١٨٠)، وصححه ابن حبان (٣٤١٣)، والضياء في المختارة (٤/١١٠).

11307 — Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever receives a favor and says to the one who did it, ‘May Allah reward you with goodness,’ has expressed the fullest possible praise.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2035), al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (180), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (3413), and narrated by al-Ḍiyāʾ in al-Mukhtārah (4/110).
